2026-01-04.headline: Cloud Native Windows Endpoints guide drops comparison content and Windows 10 support notice
2026-01-04.overview: The Intune Windows guide removed its comparison with Windows in cloud configuration, including the objectives table and links, along with its Windows 10 support notice.
2026-01-04.adminImpact: Administrators will no longer find those comparison materials or the Windows 10 support notice on the guide page. No administrator action is stated.

keyChanges.title: Guide removes tutorial comparison and Windows 10 notice
keyChanges.detail: The Cloud Native Windows Endpoints page removed the tip comparing the tutorial with Windows in cloud configuration, its objectives table and links, and the Windows 10 support notice.

2026-01-05.headline: Hotpatch guidance now details Arm64 preview prerequisites for Intune-managed Windows devices
2026-01-05.overview: The period centers on a Windows device-updates documentation rework. A new Windows quality update policy page documents Hotpatch deployment through Intune and Autopatch on Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later, while a new page covers Windows Driver updates management. The former Quality Updates Policy and Driver Updates Overview pages were removed, and many remaining edits repair links, paths, terminology, or navigation.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: For Hotpatch, verify VBS and the latest baseline release; Arm64 devices require CHPE disabled with the HotPatchRestrictions=1 registry setting and a restart. For Windows Driver updates, review enrollment, Microsoft Entra join, telemetry, Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant, endpoint access, and Intune data-collection prerequisites. If driver-update reports are required, enable the Windows diagnostic-data setting under Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data. Replace bookmarks or references to removed and renamed pages.

keyChanges.title: New policy guidance defines Hotpatch deployment and Arm64 preview requirements
keyChanges.detail: The Windows quality update policy page describes deploying Hotpatch through Intune and Autopatch on Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later. Arm64 support is in public preview and requires disabling CHPE with the HotPatchRestrictions=1 registry setting and restarting devices; the guidance also calls out VBS and the latest baseline release as prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Windows Driver updates guidance spells out approval workflows and eligibility limits
keyChanges.detail: The new page explains how to review, approve, pause, decline, and automatically deploy Windows Driver updates. It also documents licensing, subscription, network, Windows edition, and GCC environment limitations, giving administrators the criteria needed to assess supported deployments.

keyChanges.title: Driver update documentation lists telemetry and service prerequisites more explicitly
keyChanges.detail: The updated overview now lists Intune enrollment, Microsoft Entra join, enabled telemetry, a running Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant, access to required endpoints, and Intune data collection. It warns that devices without configured telemetry might install a later Windows version than the one specified.

keyChanges.title: Driver update reports now require Windows diagnostic data in Intune
keyChanges.detail: The reports guidance adds a prerequisite to enable Windows diagnostic data. The documented location is Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data, where administrators turn on the required processor-configuration setting; it may already be enabled for other reports.

keyChanges.title: Company Portal guidance adds an exact winget download command
keyChanges.detail: The Store apps documentation now provides `winget install "Company Portal" --source msstore` for downloading the Windows Company Portal app with dependencies. The downloaded files are saved to the Downloads folder by default.

2026-01-06.headline: Managed Home Screen gains two planned RBAC permissions in Intune’s February release
2026-01-06.overview: Intune’s most consequential item is a planned February RBAC change: TemporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen and RestoreManagedHomeScreen will be added to the School Administrator and Help Desk Operator built-in roles. Documentation updates also clarify Windows Feature Updates licensing and support boundaries, identify Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs as an EPM-supported platform, extend the documented audit-log window to two years, and restate the required MDT removal sequence. A new Windows Driver updates FAQ centralizes guidance on filters, Autopilot, rollback, multiple policies, reboots, driver availability, and Autopatch synchronization. Much of the remaining activity was terminology, formatting, navigation, or procedural cleanup.
2026-01-06.adminImpact: Verify Intune Plan 1 and the required Autopatch-entitled Windows licensing when planning Feature Updates, and account for the documented GCC High/DoD and LTSC limitations. For Configuration Manager, remove MDT task sequence steps before removing MDT integration. Review Managed Home Screen role assignments and internal role documentation as appropriate; no immediate action is required for that planned role update. The two-year audit-log guidance should inform security and compliance planning, while EPM administrators can use the updated supported-platform list when assessing AVD single-session deployments.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen RBAC permissions are planned for February
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s February release adds TemporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen and RestoreManagedHomeScreen to the School Administrator and Help Desk Operator built-in roles. Microsoft states that no administrator action is required, while reviewing role assignments and updating internal documentation is recommended.

keyChanges.title: Feature Updates guidance now sets licensing and support boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The guidance specifies Intune Plan 1 for core Feature Updates functionality and an Autopatch-entitled Windows license for gradual rollout and optional feature updates. It also identifies GCC High/DoD and LTSC scenarios that require alternative patching methods.

keyChanges.title: EPM support guidance now names AVD single-session virtual machines
keyChanges.detail: The supported-platform list now directly names Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines and Windows 365 for Endpoint Privilege Management policies, giving administrators clearer scope when planning virtual deployments.

keyChanges.title: Intune audit-log retention guidance now says up to two years
keyChanges.detail: The Privacy Data Store Process page now states that Intune audit logs are retained for up to two years for security purposes, instead of one year. Administrators should account for the longer documented availability in security and compliance processes.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents the required MDT removal order
keyChanges.detail: The release notes instruct administrators to remove all MDT task sequence steps before removing MDT integration. MDT remains retired and unsupported, and following this order helps prevent task sequence corruption and modification failures.

2026-01-07.headline: Windows Driver updates guidance now documents Autopatch licensing and cloud limits
2026-01-07.overview: The period is dominated by a coordinated rewrite of Intune’s Windows Driver updates material rather than broad feature announcements. A new policy reference covers review, approval, automatic deployment, pausing, and manual management, while related guidance spells out cloud, licensing, Windows-edition, and government-environment boundaries. Other substantive documentation changes classify Hotpatch within Quality updates, state that Intune audit logs are retained for up to two years, and remove the old driver FAQ; most remaining edits are link, title, navigation, formatting, or wording maintenance.
2026-01-07.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating Windows Driver updates should verify public-cloud tenancy, Intune Plan 1, the required Windows license with the Autopatch entitlement, and supported editions before configuring policies; GCC High, DoD, and LTSC are called out as unsupported. The documentation separately says existing-EA subscription activation does not apply to GCC, GCC High, or DoD, while the overview removes a blanket statement that the feature is not supported in GCC, so use the scoped guidance. The removed FAQ is no longer available for assignment-filter, Autopilot, rollback, reboot, availability, or synchronization questions. No configuration or migration action is stated for the Hotpatch/index or audit-retention edits.

keyChanges.title: Driver Updates gets a new policy-management reference
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune page describes how administrators can review, approve, automatically deploy, pause, or manually manage Windows driver updates, and includes licensing, supported Windows-edition, and deployment-behavior guidance.

keyChanges.title: Driver Updates documentation specifies tenant and license boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The Driver Updates article says policies are supported only in the public cloud and require Intune Plan 1 plus a Windows license with the Autopatch entitlement. GCC High and DoD environments are not supported, and LTSC remains unsupported.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch is grouped under Quality updates in the update index
keyChanges.detail: The Device updates index now describes Autopatch without naming WUfB DS, places Hotpatch under Quality updates, and includes Feature, Quality, and Driver updates in its Microsoft Entra registered-device limitation. It also describes Hotpatch as optional for manual quality-update management and automatic for eligible Autopatch devices.

keyChanges.title: Intune audit-log retention is stated as up to two years
keyChanges.detail: The Privacy Data Store Process page now states that Intune audit logs are retained for up to two years for security purposes, giving administrators an explicit retention period for audit-data handling.

keyChanges.title: Windows Driver updates FAQ is removed
keyChanges.detail: The removed FAQ covered assignment filters, Autopilot, rollback, policy assignments, reboots, driver availability, and Windows Autopatch synchronization. Administrators can no longer use that page as a reference for those policy questions.

2026-01-08.headline: Intune driver policies now name the settings that block Windows driver installation
2026-01-08.overview: Windows driver update policy guidance now gives administrators precise allow values to check: Windows driver = Allow in update rings and Allow Windows Update drivers in Settings Catalog policies; both allow drivers by default. The period also removes the Driver Updates Overview page, records Endpoint Privilege Management policy support for Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs as in development, and adds Enterprise Agreement and sovereign-cloud boundaries to Autopatch guidance. An iOS line-of-business app note documents manual-downgrade behavior, while most other edits consolidate prerequisites or adjust layout and navigation.
2026-01-08.adminImpact: Review applicable driver update policies against the documented values. If Enterprise Agreement licensing blocks creation of Autopatch-dependent policies, contact the licensing source; existing-EA subscription activation guidance does not apply to GCC, GCC High, or DoD environments. Treat EPM support for AVD single-session VMs as in-development planning guidance. When troubleshooting iOS available-app updates, account for manual downgrades, and note that the deleted Driver Updates Overview page is no longer available as a reference.

keyChanges.title: Driver policy guidance identifies the settings that can block installation
keyChanges.detail: The Driver Updates Policy page now specifies that update rings should use Windows driver set to Allow, while Settings Catalog policies should use Allow Windows Update drivers. Both settings allow driver updates by default.

keyChanges.title: The Windows Driver Updates Overview page was removed
keyChanges.detail: The page covering Windows driver update policies, approvals, pauses, prerequisites, and supported editions was deleted, so administrators can no longer use it as a reference.

keyChanges.title: EPM lists AVD single-session support as in development
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Privilege Management In Development page now states that EPM policies will support users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch guidance adds EA support routing and cloud boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The guidance directs administrators blocked from creating Autopatch-dependent policies with Enterprise Agreement licenses to contact their licensing source. It also states that subscription activation with an existing EA does not apply to GCC, GCC High, or DoD environments for Windows Autopatch capabilities.

keyChanges.title: iOS available-app guidance documents manual-downgrade behavior
keyChanges.detail: The iOS line-of-business app guidance now says an app targeted with available intent will not update automatically when the installed app was manually downgraded. It also clarifies terminology and bundle identifier guidance.

2026-01-09.headline: Windows update guidance adds rollout controls, Hotpatch prerequisites, and Autopatch ring rules
2026-01-09.overview: The period is led by a focused expansion of Intune guidance for Windows servicing. New feature- and quality-update policy pages cover policy assignment, rollout timing, safeguard holds, Hotpatch, expedited updates, and conflicting update settings; related ring guidance says Autopatch may create and maintain rings. Mobile Threat Defense guidance also documents optional iOS/iPadOS Certificate Sync. Many of the other edits are reviewer metadata, formatting, or terminology changes.
2026-01-09.adminImpact: For Windows servicing plans, use the feature and quality policy guidance to validate rollout design and prerequisites, check update ring and Group Policy conflicts before expedited deployments, and review custom ring assignments on Autopatch-managed devices. Treat Windows 11 version 24H2 and later as unable to apply KB 4023057. Enable iOS/iPadOS Certificate Sync in MTD connector settings when certificate inventory sharing is intended; reviewer and formatting changes require no action.

keyChanges.title: Feature update policy guidance now covers rollout timing and safeguard holds
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows feature update policies page explains how to create and assign policies, configure rollout timing, manage optional or required updates, and understand safeguard holds and multi-policy behavior. It gives administrators a documented workflow for deploying supported Windows versions and anticipating device and user update behavior.

keyChanges.title: Quality update guidance spells out Hotpatch and expedited-update prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows quality updates policy page adds prerequisites and configuration guidance for Hotpatch and expedited updates, including update ring and Group Policy settings that can interfere with installation. Administrators should validate those settings before deployment.

keyChanges.title: Expedited-update guidance records a Windows 11 24H2 KB limitation
keyChanges.detail: The expedited updates article now states that Windows 11 version 24H2 and later cannot apply KB 4023057. It also reorganizes prerequisite material and separates Update Health Tools guidance, giving servicing teams a specific compatibility constraint for update planning.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch guidance warns against custom rings on managed devices
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Update rings policy guidance says Windows Autopatch may create and maintain rings, and that administrators typically shouldn't assign custom rings to Autopatch-managed devices. Review ring assignments where Autopatch coordinates updates.

keyChanges.title: Mobile Threat Defense guidance adds optional iOS/iPadOS Certificate Sync detail
keyChanges.detail: The updated Mobile Threat Defense guidance documents optional Certificate Sync through MTD connectors for iOS/iPadOS. It covers certificate inventory sharing for corporate and personally owned devices, the certificate data sent, and how connector status affects synchronization requests. To share inventory, enable Certificate Sync in the connector settings.

2026-01-12.headline: Intune Win32 apps gain uploaded PowerShell scripts for installation
2026-01-12.overview: The clearest capability change is in Win32 app creation: administrators can upload a PowerShell script instead of specifying a command line, with Intune packaging and running it in the app installer’s context. The broader period refreshes Windows Update guidance with actionable detail on expedited quality updates, feature-update policy transitions, Autopilot provisioning, and a newly documented OOBE update-scan failure mode.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Prioritize testing the new Win32 script workflow and any Enterprise App Catalog script overrides. For Windows servicing, verify Update Health Tools coverage on pre-24H2 devices, account for feature-update policy and Autopatch behavior, and use the Autopilot known issue when diagnosing provisioning results. The supplied feature-update guidance states no mandatory administrator deadline.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app creation accepts PowerShell installation scripts
keyChanges.detail: The What's New entry says administrators can upload a PowerShell script instead of specifying a command line when adding a Windows Win32 app. Intune packages the script with the app content and runs it in the app installer’s context, enabling workflows such as prerequisite checks and configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Feature Updates guidance clarifies Autopilot and Autopatch behavior
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance covers update-ring settings, paused updates, Autopilot provisioning timing, group validation, and automatic Windows Autopatch enrollment. It states that devices remain enrolled in Autopatch after policy removal and receive no feature update until reassigned or explicitly unenrolled. Administrators should review overlapping rings and policy application after Autopilot provisioning.

keyChanges.title: Quality Updates policies document expedited security servicing prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The article explains how Quality Updates policies deploy eligible Windows security updates without changing monthly update policies. Devices running Windows versions before 24H2 require Update Health Tools; the guidance also covers update selection, deferral overrides, and restart behavior. Expedited policies can be used for urgent security updates while update rings handle regular servicing.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot OOBE quality-update scans may time out on newer devices
keyChanges.detail: A new known issue affects devices with KB5041571 and later when Allow OOBE Updates is enabled in the Enrollment Status Page profile. Quality Update scans may time out during OOBE, leaving updates uninstalled during provisioning. The issue is under investigation, so administrators should account for this outcome when troubleshooting deployments.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog scripts require post-creation changes with MAA
keyChanges.detail: PowerShell script overrides replace the standard install and uninstall commands. In tenants with Multi-Admin Approval enabled, scripts cannot be uploaded during app creation; they must be added or modified afterward. When no Microsoft Entra user is present, the scripts run in system context. Administrators should create the app first in MAA-enabled tenants and test the override behavior.

2026-01-13.headline: Hotpatch guidance adds Autopatch deployment rules and Arm64 CHPE prerequisites
2026-01-13.overview: Intune’s 13 January material centers on Windows update administration. New guidance explains Hotpatch deployment through Windows Autopatch, fallback for ineligible devices, reporting, and Arm64 public-preview prerequisites. A separate Windows quality updates policy page documents expedited-update conflicts and pre-24H2 tooling requirements. Related updates sharpen driver approval governance, Hotpatch reporting, and Defender compliance workflows; many remaining edits are navigation, terminology, and link maintenance.
2026-01-13.adminImpact: For Hotpatch, verify VBS and Autopatch prerequisites; Arm64 preview devices also require CHPE to be disabled and a restart. Before using expedited quality updates, check update-ring and Group Policy conflicts, set listed conflicting policies to Not configured, and verify Update Health Tools on Windows versions earlier than 24H2. Driver-policy owners should establish approval and phased-rollout processes, assign each device to one policy, and explicitly approve updates when using manual approval.

keyChanges.title: New Hotpatch guidance ties deployment to Autopatch and eligibility rules
keyChanges.detail: The new guide explains Hotpatch release cycles, reporting, prerequisites, and fallback to cumulative updates for ineligible devices. VBS is required for eligible devices; Autopatch is required for deployment. Arm64 support is identified as public preview and requires CHPE to be disabled and the device restarted.

keyChanges.title: Windows quality updates policy guidance defines expedited-update prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new policy page documents expedited security update deployment, release-date targeting, applicability, and conflicts with update rings and Group Policy. Update Health Tools are required on Windows versions earlier than 24H2.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch reporting guidance adds a specific Intune admin-center path
keyChanges.detail: For policies with Hotpatch enabled, administrators are directed to Reports > Windows Autopatch > Windows quality updates > Reports to review deployment status, results, errors, targeted devices, and current update states.

keyChanges.title: Driver policy guidance formalizes ownership, rollout, and approval controls
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance covers approval ownership, phased deployments, update cadence, automatic versus manual approval, approved-driver selection, Autopatch fallback, and pausing or reapproving drivers. Each device should be assigned to one policy, with updates explicitly approved when manual approval is used.

keyChanges.title: Defender integration guidance reorganizes compliance and risk-based access setup
keyChanges.detail: The updated workflow emphasizes device compliance, real-time risk assessment, and automatic blocking of compromised devices. It presents a four-step integration process, adds a role-assignment tip, and reorganizes vulnerability-management and app-protection options.

2026-01-14.headline: Expedite-policy guidance covers targeted Windows security updates beyond normal deferrals
2026-01-14.overview: Windows update servicing is the period’s substantive theme. Intune added a dedicated Expedite Policies guidance page explaining acceleration of a specific supported Windows security update beyond normal deferrals and deployment timing, including creation, assignment, monitoring, prerequisites, and eligibility; the older Expedite Quality Updates page was deleted. Related guidance now makes feature-update persistence, no-downgrade behavior, and staged or intelligent rollout prerequisites explicit. Win32 app guidance also documents PowerShell script installers, while the Windows Driver Updates page removes approval and recommended-driver instructions. Remaining title, terminology, RBAC, and metadata edits are mostly editorial.
2026-01-14.adminImpact: Administrators handling urgent security remediation should verify expedite prerequisites, configure update-ring settings, remove conflicting Group Policy settings, and ensure Update Health Tools are installed on Windows versions earlier than 24H2. For feature updates, account for policies persisting until changed or removed, no downgrades for devices already on newer versions, and optional versus required updates. Staged rollout planning should include offer-group spacing; intelligent rollout requires enabling Windows Update for Business Cloud Processing in a settings catalog profile. With Multi-Admin Approval, create a Win32 app before adding or modifying a PowerShell installer script. Teams relying on the deleted expedite page or removed driver-approval guidance should review current Int

keyChanges.title: Expedite Policies guidance details targeted security-update acceleration
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune page documents policies that accelerate a specific supported Windows security update, bypass normal deferrals and deployment timing, and cover creation, assignment, monitoring, prerequisites, and eligibility. It also calls for verifying update-ring settings, removing conflicting Group Policy settings, and installing Update Health Tools on Windows versions earlier than 24H2.

keyChanges.title: The older Expedite Quality Updates page was removed
keyChanges.detail: The former Intune page covering expedited Windows security updates, prerequisites, Update Health Tools, and policy behavior was deleted. Administrators relying on that URL will no longer find its guidance there.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update guidance clarifies persistence and no-downgrade behavior
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance states that version-targeting policies persist until changed or removed, do not downgrade devices already on newer versions, and include the latest applicable monthly quality update. It also clarifies optional versus required updates and how multiple policies are evaluated.

keyChanges.title: Rollout Options guidance adds staged offers and intelligent-rollout prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance adds gradual-rollout configuration, offer-group behavior, examples, and intelligent rollout using Windows Autopatch telemetry and safeguard holds. Intelligent rollout requires enabling Windows Update for Business Cloud Processing in a settings catalog profile.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app guidance documents a PowerShell script installer procedure
keyChanges.detail: The workflow now covers uploading a PowerShell script instead of an install command. Scripts run in the installer context, support prerequisite and post-install actions, are limited to 50 KB, and use return codes for status. With Multi-Admin Approval, create the app first, then add or modify the script.

2026-01-15.headline: Edge for Business guidance separates enrollment policy paths and adds data-security troubleshooting
2026-01-15.overview: The period was mostly documentation maintenance—terminology, links, formatting, and page restructuring—but several changes have direct administrative value. Secure Enterprise Browser guidance now distinguishes policy paths by enrollment status and adds related troubleshooting material, while Windows update guidance sharpens rollout timing and introduces driver-policy procedures. Azure Monitor guidance also adds a concrete expectation for Intune data availability.
2026-01-15.adminImpact: Review Secure Enterprise Browser assignments against the revised enrollment-based guidance: avoid targeting the same client with both App Configuration and Settings Catalog policies, and on enrolled Windows devices choose either Settings Catalog or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline. Before deploying driver update policies, verify the stated prerequisites and driver-installation controls. Allow up to 48 hours when troubleshooting missing Azure Monitor data.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business policy guidance now distinguishes enrolled and non-enrolled clients
keyChanges.detail: The revised Secure Enterprise Browser sequence maps App Configuration Policies to non-enrolled devices and Settings Catalog policies to enrolled devices. It removes the Security Baseline deployment step from the sequence, says enrolled Windows devices should use either Settings Catalog or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline—not both—and warns against targeting one client with both App Configuration and Settings Catalog policies.

keyChanges.title: A new Edge for Business step adds data-security troubleshooting coverage
keyChanges.detail: The new Step 7 covers policy assignments, settings, sign-in, app and platform requirements, configuration channels, policy conflicts, and platform-specific issues. It gives administrators checks and resolutions for diagnosing app protection and app configuration policy deployment or enforcement problems.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update rollout guidance separates availability from installation timing
keyChanges.detail: The revised rollout article explains three availability behaviors, offer groups, and rollout scheduling, while distinguishing when an update is offered from when installation occurs. Installation timing depends on controls such as deadlines and restart settings, giving administrators clearer guidance for gradual deployments.

keyChanges.title: Windows driver update guidance adds approval, pause, and deployment procedures
keyChanges.detail: The new how-to covers prerequisites, automatic or manual driver approval, pausing and reapproving updates, and deployment behavior. It advises checking that update-ring and Settings Catalog policies allow driver installation and avoiding assignments that place devices in multiple driver update policies.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor guidance sets a 24-hour cadence and 48-hour data window
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance states that Device Compliance Organizational Logs and Intune Devices report data is sent once every 24 hours, with export occurring during each 24-hour period and taking up to 48 hours overall. This sets the expected wait when investigating missing data.

2026-01-16.headline: Network-denial policy blocks local Autopilot Reset; Intune clarifies Edge and update guidance
2026-01-16.overview: The clearest operational change is a newly documented Windows Autopilot known issue: an Intune policy that denies network access to the Local account prevents local Windows administrators from initiating a local Autopilot Reset. Other high-value edits sharpen how administrators target quality updates, choose Microsoft Edge policy paths, interpret Azure Monitor freshness, and satisfy RBAC prerequisites.
2026-01-16.adminImpact: If local administrators are expected to trigger resets, review the named network-denial setting and use the documented workaround of removing it while Microsoft investigates. Also review Edge assignments, separate quality-update targeting from ring and client behavior, allow for the documented Azure Monitor delays, and use the revised role prerequisites in affected quickstarts.

keyChanges.title: Local Autopilot Reset is blocked by a specific network-denial setting
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot known-issues entry says that when an Intune policy sets “Deny access to this computer from the network” for the Local account, local Windows administrators cannot initiate a local Windows Autopilot Reset. The issue is under investigation; removing the setting is the documented workaround.

keyChanges.title: Quality Updates guidance separates update targeting from client behavior
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now describes targeting specific quality updates and states that restart settings, deadlines, notifications, and deferrals remain configured through update rings and Windows Update client policies. Use quality update policies for targeting or expediting, and the existing ring and client policy settings for client-side behavior.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Edge policy paths are explicitly separated by enrollment status
keyChanges.detail: The Edge overview now states that App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies targeting Microsoft Edge shouldn’t both be deployed to the same client because they can conflict. Non-enrolled devices use App Configuration Policies, while enrolled devices use Settings Catalog policies.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor guidance now gives precise report-delivery timings
keyChanges.detail: The documentation says Intune report data is sent to Azure Monitor once every 24 hours, may take up to an additional 24 hours to arrive, and typically appears within 30 minutes after Azure Monitor receives it. Use these timings when setting expectations for log availability and report freshness.

keyChanges.title: Noncompliance email guidance now requires the Policy and Profile manager role
keyChanges.detail: The quickstart now lists an Intune subscription and the built-in Policy and Profile manager role as requirements, replacing the previous Intune Administrator guidance. It also removes the prior compliance-partner limitation; administrators following the guide should verify the revised role requirement.

2026-01-20.headline: Managed Home Screen remote actions gain documented Android scope and permissions
2026-01-20.overview: The period’s most consequential Intune guidance changes clarify remote Managed Home Screen operations, tighten the documented app-protection assignment requirement, and record Windows quality-update enforcement in Enrollment Status Page guidance. The remaining updates are primarily navigation, terminology, formatting, and setup-documentation refinements.
2026-01-20.adminImpact: Review the Managed Home Screen action guidance if you administer Android Enterprise corporate-owned devices or automate these operations. When creating app protection policies, assign a group containing users rather than devices. Also account for the documented OS enforcement associated with the Install Windows quality updates setting in the 2026-01 B quality update.

keyChanges.title: Restore Managed Home Screen guidance defines supported Android modes and permissions
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance identifies Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) devices as supported, names the required permission as “Remote tasks/Restore Managed Home Screen,” and provides an updated Microsoft Graph reference for automation.

keyChanges.title: Suspend Managed Home Screen guidance adds the supported device scope
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now specifies Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) devices, identifies the required permission, and updates the Microsoft Graph API reference for the suspend action.

keyChanges.title: App protection assignments explicitly require a users group
keyChanges.detail: Step 9 now directs administrators to select the users group and states inline that groups containing devices cannot be used for app protection policies.

keyChanges.title: Enrollment Status Page guidance records 2026-01 B quality-update enforcement
keyChanges.detail: The article now states that OS enforcement for the Install Windows quality updates Intune setting is included in the 2026-01 B quality update. Administrators managing Windows quality-update settings should account for that documented enforcement.

2026-01-21.headline: Intune guided scenarios leave the admin center in March, except Windows 365 Boot
2026-01-21.overview: The most consequential update is a March 2026 notice that all Intune guided scenarios except Windows 365 Boot will be removed from the Intune admin center. Existing configurations are unaffected and Microsoft says no administrator action is required. The remaining updates are chiefly documentation maintenance, with practical guidance added for Win32 .msu deployment, missed custom notifications, trial-license verification, and role assignment.
2026-01-21.adminImpact: No immediate change is required for existing guided-scenario configurations. Administrators evaluating Win32 application deployment for .msu updates should note that Microsoft now marks that method as not recommended. When troubleshooting missed custom notifications, review battery optimization for the Company Portal or Intune app. Trial setup guidance now provides links for confirming licenses and assigning built-in roles.

keyChanges.title: Guided scenarios will be removed in March 2026
keyChanges.detail: Starting in March 2026, all Intune guided scenarios except Windows 365 Boot will be removed from the Intune admin center. Existing configurations remain unaffected, no administrator action is needed, and Microsoft provides alternative guidance resources.

keyChanges.title: Win32 guidance cautions against deploying .msu updates
keyChanges.detail: The Apps Win32 Deploy Update Package guidance now says deploying .msu updates using the application method is not recommended and that the guidance is provided as-is.

keyChanges.title: Battery optimization is identified as a cause of missed custom notifications
keyChanges.detail: The Custom Notifications guidance now notes that battery optimization on some devices can prevent delivery and suggests disabling optimization for the Company Portal or Intune app to improve reliability.

keyChanges.title: Free-trial guidance adds license and role-assignment links
keyChanges.detail: The Free Trial Sign Up documentation now directs administrators to confirm trial licenses after configuration, clarifies Intune admin center responsibilities, and links to built-in role assignment guidance.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen restore documentation uses current API references
keyChanges.detail: The restore guidance now points to the current managedDevice resource and restoreManagedHomeScreen action references.

2026-01-22.headline: Conditional Access approved-client control retires in June; adopt application protection policies
2026-01-22.overview: The period’s most consequential change is the announced June 2026 retirement of the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control. Intune’s migration guidance also clarifies the license-driven transition from Basic Mobility and Security, while Windows update and macOS Platform SSO guidance received more targeted procedural updates.
2026-01-22.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that use “Require approved client app” and move them to “Require application protection policy” before June 2026, because the retired control will no longer be enforceable. For migrations from Basic Mobility and Security, map policies, assign Intune licenses with the management transition in mind, and review or remove legacy policies to avoid unintended future assignments. Administrators following the Windows or macOS guidance should use the updated policy recommendations and terminology.

keyChanges.title: Approved-client Conditional Access control scheduled for June retirement
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access will retire the “Require approved client app” control in June 2026. Microsoft recommends replacing it with “Require application protection policy,” which provides equivalent and enhanced protection; after retirement, the old control will no longer be enforceable.

keyChanges.title: Intune licensing now documented as the Basic Mobility and Security handoff
keyChanges.detail: The migration guide states that assigning Intune licenses switches users to Intune management and that Basic Mobility and Security policies no longer apply to users assigned Intune. It adds policy-mapping and license-assignment guidance and recommends removing old policies.

keyChanges.title: Windows update guidance favors update policies over Win32 app deployment
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Windows Update Packages in Intune article now recommends Windows Update policies—including update rings, feature updates, and quality updates—instead of deploying updates as Win32 apps. The change is guidance for administrators planning .msu deployments; no required configuration change is stated.

keyChanges.title: macOS Platform SSO guidance now recommends enforcement during registration
keyChanges.detail: The macOS endpoints guide updates its Platform SSO wording and revises the recommendation to enforce Platform SSO during device registration. The related wording identifies Platform SSO as a Zero Trust best practice; no required administrator action is stated.

2026-01-23.headline: Microsoft Defender for Android ends enrolled personal-profile protection by March 2026
2026-01-23.overview: Microsoft Defender for Android will end support for protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices by March 2026, focusing on corporate work profiles. Work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected, and Microsoft says no administrator action is required. The period’s other useful changes refine Intune migration, Advanced Analytics query syntax, and Remediations delivery guidance.
2026-01-23.adminImpact: No administrative change is specified for the Defender transition. Migration teams should use the updated role and policy-removal guidance; query authors should apply the corrected scalar Device-property syntax; and administrators sending Run remediation actions should account for device connectivity to Intune or WNS.

keyChanges.title: Personal-profile protection ends for enrolled Android devices
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center says Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices by March 2026 and focus on corporate work profiles. Work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected, and the notice requires no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Intune migration guidance names required roles and policy cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The migration guide now instructs administrators to assign licenses and policies, identifies the Endpoint Security Manager and Conditional Access Administrator roles, and links to role details and guidance for removing unneeded Basic Mobility and Security policies.

keyChanges.title: Device Query guidance adds join types and scalar-property rules
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Analytics documentation now lists nine supported join types, adding leftsemi, rightsemi, leftanti, and rightanti. It also clarifies that Device must be referenced through a scalar property, such as Device.DeviceId, for operators including distinct, summarize, and order by, with corrected aggregation examples.

keyChanges.title: Remediations guidance ties Run delivery to connectivity
keyChanges.detail: The Remediations page now states that a device will not receive the Run remediation action when it is offline or cannot communicate successfully with Intune or WNS when the action is sent. Administrators should account for connectivity when issuing the action.

2026-01-24.headline: Device Query guidance favors scalar properties for distinct, summarize, and order by
2026-01-24.overview: Advanced Analytics updates center on the Device Query Multiple Devices reference. It now recommends specific scalar device properties such as `Device.SerialNumber` and `Device.OSVersion` for queries using `distinct`, `summarize`, and `order by`; the same reference continues to identify `innerunique` as the default join type.
2026-01-24.adminImpact: Query authors should use a specific scalar device property with those operators and consult the revised join reference. No configuration change is indicated.

keyChanges.title: Scalar-property guidance added for common query operators
keyChanges.detail: The reference recommends using scalar device properties, including `Device.SerialNumber` or `Device.OSVersion`, with `distinct`, `summarize`, and `order by`.

keyChanges.title: Join reference retains supported types and default
keyChanges.detail: The edited `join` operator entry continues to list the supported join types and specifies `innerunique` as the default.

2026-01-26.headline: Cloud PKI guidance adds BYOCA, CA setup, and certificate lifecycle procedures
2026-01-26.overview: The period is dominated by a reorganized Microsoft Intune Cloud PKI guidance set. New articles cover deployment models, root and issuing CA configuration, BYOCA, audit logs, monitoring, and certificate-authority deletion, while older page paths and associated links or images were removed or relocated. Outside Cloud PKI, Windows Autopilot device preparation now documents a 25-app OOBE limit in both modes, and Intune’s Mobile Threat Defense guidance changes two threat-level mappings for the Block access action.
2026-01-26.adminImpact: Cloud PKI administrators should use the current linked pages rather than older file paths and apply the documented RBAC, trust-chain, CA-ordering, and deletion requirements when planning changes. Autopilot administrators can plan for up to 25 managed applications during device preparation. Administrators using MTD with Block access should review the updated threat-level mappings in affected configurations.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI documents Microsoft-rooted and BYOCA deployment models
keyChanges.detail: The deployment guidance covers two models: a Microsoft Cloud PKI root CA or BYOCA using a private CA. It also documents trust-chain prerequisites and distributing CA certificates to relying parties.

keyChanges.title: New Cloud PKI procedures specify root and issuing CA configuration
keyChanges.detail: The configuration article covers prerequisites and RBAC permissions, along with validity, EKU, subject, encryption, and scope-tag settings. It requires creating a root CA before an issuing CA.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI deletion guidance defines the CA removal sequence
keyChanges.detail: The new procedure covers pausing, revoking, and permanently deleting issuing and root CAs. Root CAs can be deleted only after their anchored issuing CAs are removed, and the guidance calls out required permissions and irreversible steps.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot device preparation raises the documented OOBE app limit to 25
keyChanges.detail: The current guidance says the limit increased from 10 to 25 managed applications for installation during OOBE, applying to both user-driven and automatic modes.

keyChanges.title: MTD Block access mappings now use High and Low threat levels
keyChanges.detail: The integration guidance now lists High instead of Low, and Low instead of Medium, for configurations that use the Block access action.

2026-01-27.headline: Settings catalog (DDM) filters marked unsupported as Intune enrollment guidance shifts admin roles
2026-01-27.overview: The 27 January set is a documentation-led correction and role-guidance pass. The Filters Supported Workloads page now marks Settings catalog (DDM) as unsupported in two workload entries, while Windows enrollment and automatic-enrollment instructions now name the built-in Intune Administrator role instead of Microsoft Entra Global Administrator. App Protection monitoring guidance also adds prerequisites and clarifies policy visibility by administrator scope.
2026-01-27.adminImpact: Review filters targeting Settings catalog (DDM) against the revised support entries. For Windows enrollment and automatic enrollment, use the Intune Administrator role where the affected guides specify it and check the referenced licensing and RBAC prerequisites. Use the updated App Protection guidance when verifying policy visibility for scoped administrators and Global Administrators.

keyChanges.title: Settings catalog (DDM) is marked unsupported in two filter workload entries
keyChanges.detail: The Filters Supported Workloads page now marks Settings catalog (DDM) as unsupported in two workload entries. Administrators reviewing filters that target this workload should validate their configurations against the revised support entries.

keyChanges.title: Windows enrollment prerequisites now use the built-in Intune Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Windows Enroll replaces its Requirements section with Prerequisites, adds licensing and RBAC references plus trial links, and changes the listed role from Microsoft Entra Global Administrator to the built-in Intune Administrator role.

keyChanges.title: Automatic Enrollment setup guidance now assigns the task to Intune Administrator
keyChanges.detail: Free Trial Sign Up now says the Intune Administrator role can set up Automatic Enrollment for Windows devices, removes the separate Global Administrator entry for that task, and suggests signing out of the Global Administrator account before continuing.

keyChanges.title: App Protection monitoring adds prerequisites and clarifies role-based policy visibility
keyChanges.detail: How to Monitor App Protection Policies adds a Before you begin section and Global Administrator guidance, and clarifies policy visibility for scoped administrators and Global Administrators.

keyChanges.title: Free Trial guidance now documents Policy and Profile Manager coverage
keyChanges.detail: The guide now states that the Policy and Profile Manager role can manage compliance, device configuration, and most enrollment policies, giving administrators clearer information when assessing or assigning the role.

2026-01-28.headline: Configuration Manager log guidance clarifies modern-component scope and troubleshooting references
2026-01-28.overview: The period was quiet for Intune administrators: all 92 supplied updates concern Configuration Manager documentation, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. Most changes are metadata cleanup, while the substantive updates improve the Log Files reference, update Microsoft Entra ID terminology, clarify log coverage, and add or refine troubleshooting entries.
2026-01-28.adminImpact: No Intune policy, enrollment, deployment, or rollout action is indicated. Configuration Manager administrators troubleshooting logs should use the revised references and account for the documented distinction between native-code and modern managed-code components. The metadata-only edits require no action.

keyChanges.title: Log Files adds and clarifies troubleshooting references
keyChanges.detail: The Log Files article updates navigation and Microsoft Entra ID terminology and adds or clarifies entries for distmgr.log, ntsvrdis.log, ExternalEventAgent.log, and AssetAdvisor.log.

keyChanges.title: Log settings scope is tied to native-code components
keyChanges.detail: The guidance specifies that the documented settings apply to native-code components, including most older site server components, and excludes modern managed-code components such as SMS_MESSAGE_PROCESSING_ENGINE and SMS_ISVUPDATES_SYNCAGENT.

keyChanges.title: Modern-component log naming guidance becomes more precise
keyChanges.detail: The documentation states that the settings don't apply to modern components and that their log names are usually longer than eight characters and may contain underscores.

keyChanges.title: Named anchors replace autogenerated Log Files links
keyChanges.detail: The Log Files article replaces autogenerated table-of-contents anchors with named section anchors for client, server, and functionality topics, making direct navigation to those log-file sections clearer.

keyChanges.title: Metadata cleanup dominates the remaining updates
keyChanges.detail: The other updates are largely page-metadata changes; for example, the CheckDecommissionState Method page removed seven service, asset, author, manager, and localization metadata fields. No administrator action is required for that change.

2026-01-29.headline: Intune guidance replaces legacy Windows 10 prerequisites with supported-version references
2026-01-29.overview: The period was dominated by Microsoft Learn maintenance, with a clear shift away from hard-coded Windows 10 build requirements across app-management guidance. The most consequential updates add a Windows MAM connector minimum, expand Defender for Endpoint integration workflows, clarify Configuration Manager SQL settings, and align a Windows app quickstart with the current admin-center path.
2026-01-29.adminImpact: Update internal runbooks and eligibility checks to use the supported Windows versions guidance instead of legacy version numbers. For Windows MAM, account for the documented Windows 11 version 22631 (23H2) or later requirement for the MTD Connector. Use the revised Defender and Configuration Manager procedures when configuring or validating those integrations; most remaining edits are link, naming, or metadata maintenance.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app guidance moves from fixed Windows 10 builds to supported versions
keyChanges.detail: The Win32 app management prerequisite now links to supported Windows versions instead of requiring Windows 10 version 1607 or later. Delivery Optimization wording now applies to Windows devices rather than Windows 10 version 1709 and later clients. Review target-device eligibility against the linked support list.

keyChanges.title: Windows MAM guidance adds the MTD Connector minimum and updated terminology
keyChanges.detail: The Windows MAM page replaces specific Windows build and KB requirements with a supported-Windows-versions link, renames Windows Security Center to Windows Security app, and documents that the MTD Connector requires Windows 11 version 22631 (23H2) or later.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint integration guidance gains workflow-specific prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The integration guide now provides step-by-step workflows, task-specific prerequisites, and navigation for service connections, device onboarding, compliance, Conditional Access, app protection, and Security Management. It also covers unenrolled and Linux devices, helping administrators select the workflow relevant to their environment.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager SQL guidance now lists required database settings
keyChanges.detail: The SQL Server support article now lists required SQL Server and database settings, canonical names, required values, and reference links for standalone primary sites, hierarchies, and SQL Always On configurations. Administrators can use the tables for verification and should not alter database options unless directed by Microsoft support.

keyChanges.title: Windows app protection quickstart adopts the current Intune navigation
keyChanges.detail: The quickstart now directs administrators to Apps > Windows > Create instead of Apps > Protection > Create > Windows in the Microsoft Intune admin center.

2026-01-30.headline: Configuration Manager checklists now require .NET Framework 4.8 on infrastructure
2026-01-30.overview: Several Configuration Manager update checklists now specify .NET Framework 4.8 for site servers, specified site systems, and the console; the clarified Update 2509 entry keeps clients at .NET 4.6.2. The period also brings a higher Windows Autopilot OOBE app limit, more precise Intune Edge Copilot policy guidance, and a changed supported-app inventory. Most remaining records are documentation maintenance, including removal of the Restore and Suspend Managed Home Screen articles and index entries.
2026-01-30.adminImpact: Before Configuration Manager setup or upgrade, verify .NET 4.8 on applicable site servers, specified site systems, and consoles, then restart them; the clarified 2509 guidance does not require clients to move beyond .NET 4.6.2. For Intune and Autopilot, review affected Edge policy paths and CopilotMode behavior, reassess Microsoft Lists MAM assumptions, and update runbooks that depend on the removed Managed Home Screen pages.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager prerequisites distinguish infrastructure from clients
keyChanges.detail: The Update 2509 checklist now lists .NET Framework 4.8 for site servers, specific site systems, and the console, while clients require .NET Framework 4.6.2. The guidance says to update .NET and restart before running setup.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot OOBE policies can deliver up to 25 apps
keyChanges.detail: Device preparation policies can configure up to 25 apps for delivery during OOBE in both user-driven and automatic modes, giving deployment administrators a larger app-delivery capacity.

keyChanges.title: Edge Copilot settings now depend on CopilotMode state
keyChanges.detail: The Manage Microsoft Edge guidance places Copilot settings in different locations when CopilotMode is on or off, adds the Copilot prompts card setting, and documents that CopilotMode defaults to true while false prevents users from enabling Copilot Mode features.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Lists leaves the documented supported Intune app list
keyChanges.detail: The supported Microsoft Intune apps page no longer includes Microsoft Lists for iOS or Android. Administrators reviewing MAM coverage should no longer treat that page as listing Microsoft Lists as supported.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen remote-action guidance was removed
keyChanges.detail: The Restore Managed Home Screen and Suspend Managed Home Screen pages were deleted, and the Remote actions index no longer lists either action. The removed articles had covered supported platforms, prerequisites, admin-center steps, user experience, and API references.

2026-01-31.headline: Cloud PKI expiration guidance now requires replacement CAs and SCEP URI updates
2026-01-31.overview: The period’s most consequential guidance covers Cloud PKI issuing-CA expiration and certificate continuity. Microsoft now documents the replacement-CA and dependent-profile update procedure, clarifies that SCEP URI changes do not reissue certificates, and expands Endpoint Privilege Management guidance on child-process elevation behavior.
2026-01-31.adminImpact: Cloud PKI administrators should create a replacement issuing CA with matching properties and update every dependent SCEP certificate profile to the new SCEP URI before expiration; otherwise, new certificate issuance may stop and affect connectivity or certificate-based authentication. Updating the URI does not reissue existing certificates. EPM administrators should assess the security implications of each child-process option, particularly because allowing elevated child processes skips rule evaluation and deny rules.

keyChanges.title: Expiring issuing CAs now have a documented replacement path
keyChanges.detail: Cloud PKI guidance says to create a new issuing CA with matching properties and update every dependent SCEP certificate profile to the replacement CA’s SCEP URI. Without those updates, new certificates may stop being issued after expiration, affecting connectivity and certificate-based authentication.

keyChanges.title: SCEP URI replacement is documented as non-reissuing
keyChanges.detail: The expanded Cloud PKI expiration guidance clarifies that replacing the SCEP URI in associated profiles does not trigger certificate reissuance. It also explains the impact of an expiring issuing CA and the steps for creating its replacement.

keyChanges.title: EPM child-process elevation can bypass rule evaluation
keyChanges.detail: Endpoint Privilege Management guidance now explains that allowing elevated child processes skips rule evaluation and deny rules. It also cautions against overly broad rules for applications that launch other processes when administrators choose among the three child-process options.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI renewal guidance says not to add more SCEP URIs
keyChanges.detail: The renewal guidance now says “Don’t add more SCEP URIs,” and changes the “Additional diagnostics” heading to “More diagnostics.” The supplied administrator impact identifies this as wording guidance with no required action.

2026-02-02.headline: In-development listings cover wired 802.1X for iPadOS and MAC controls for macOS
2026-02-02.overview: The period was documentation-led: the Intune In Development page now describes upcoming platform controls, while other updates clarify Zebra Android permissions, Android app-protection offline guidance, and custom-role permissions. A separate metadata-only update does not add administrator-facing substance.
2026-02-02.adminImpact: Review the in-development networking controls when planning secure iPad Ethernet access or macOS networks that require stable MAC addresses. Zebra administrators should verify the newly documented permissions, and administrators configuring offline access or custom roles should use the revised guidance and permission entries.

keyChanges.title: Upcoming iOS/iPadOS and macOS networking controls
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page now describes an 802.1X Wired Networks profile for iOS/iPadOS 17+ and a macOS 15+ setting to disable MAC address randomization. Several older in-development entries were also removed. These listings are relevant to planning secure iPad Ethernet access and networks that require stable MAC addresses.

keyChanges.title: Zebra Managed Home Screen permissions now name two required grants
keyChanges.detail: The Android OEMConfig permissions table identifies Alarms & Reminders and Write Settings as required for Zebra devices using the listed Managed Home Screen features: screen saver, sign-out, relaunch, brightness, and rotation. Zebra administrators can use the entries to verify device permissions.

keyChanges.title: Android app-protection guidance revises offline grace-period wording
keyChanges.detail: The Offline grace period description and its accompanying note were updated. Administrators configuring offline access for managed apps should consult the revised Android app-protection policy guidance.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role tables now document device-management CRUD permissions
keyChanges.detail: The custom-role permissions table now documents Create, Delete, Read, and Update permissions for device-management administrative tasks, alongside related table ordering and formatting changes. Administrators defining Intune custom roles can reference these entries when assigning permissions.

2026-02-03.headline: Intune service guidance now uses endpoint management instead of enterprise mobility management
2026-02-03.overview: The period brought targeted updates to Intune service, RBAC, and mobile Edge guidance. The service description now uses endpoint-management terminology, refreshes supported-device, app, and integration language, and removes its stated 100-user trial limit. Other substantive edits document current custom-role permissions, service-notice locations, RBAC lookup labels, and PAC failure behavior in Edge for iOS and Android. Remaining changes are mainly metadata, wording, link, or presentation cleanup.
2026-02-03.adminImpact: Use the revised service description when communicating Intune scope, integrations, and trial offerings. Review current permission and action references when creating or auditing roles, monitor notices through the documented admin-center paths, and check Edge PAC policies against the stated default and failed-open option. No configuration change is indicated by the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Service terminology and scope language now use endpoint management
keyChanges.detail: The Service Description changes Intune’s description from enterprise mobility management to endpoint management, clarifies supported devices and apps and integration wording, and removes the article’s stated 100-user trial limit. Administrators should use the revised article for current scope, integration, and trial communications.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role guidance lists current permission and action coverage
keyChanges.detail: The Create Custom Role page now reflects the current Intune UI and lists permissions for cloud-attached devices, Cloud PKI, Deployment Plans, and Android Enterprise enrollment-time membership assignment. Review the updated permission and action list when creating or auditing custom roles.

keyChanges.title: Edge mobile guidance documents a PAC fail-closed default
keyChanges.detail: For Microsoft Edge on iOS and Android, invalid or unavailable PAC scripts block network access by default; organizations can change the behavior to PAC failed-open. Administrators reviewing PAC policies should use this documented default and option.

keyChanges.title: Service-notice paths now cover both admin centers
keyChanges.detail: The service description directs administrators to Intune at Tenant administration > Tenant status > Service health and message center, and to Microsoft 365 at Health > Message center. It also updates guidance for the Microsoft 365 Admin mobile app and Message Center.

keyChanges.title: RBAC lookup guidance adopts Permission and Action labels
keyChanges.detail: The Role Based Access Control guidance now instructs administrators to identify entries by Permission and Action instead of Category and Permission. This aligns the lookup instructions with the current Intune admin center terminology.

2026-02-04.headline: Intune guidance documents EPM elevation policies for AVD single-session VMs
2026-02-04.overview: The period was dominated by documentation maintenance, but the February 2 Intune update records several substantive capability entries: EPM elevation policies for users on AVD single-session VMs, a Lenovo Device Orchestration link, four newly available protected apps, and new Windows settings catalog policies. Configuration Manager guidance adds concrete SQL support, compatibility, security, and authentication details. Other Intune edits primarily affect roadmap visibility, reviewer metadata, and reference-table presentation.
2026-02-04.adminImpact: Intune administrators can evaluate the documented EPM, protected-app, Lenovo, and Windows policy options as relevant. Roadmap readers should note that six items were removed from the In development page. Configuration Manager administrators should review SQL version and compatibility requirements, consider Extended Protection guidance, and use the clarified CMG management-point authentication procedures. No action is indicated for the metadata-only edits.

keyChanges.title: February Intune guidance records EPM and new policy options
keyChanges.detail: The February 2 update documents EPM elevation policies for users on AVD single-session VMs, a Lenovo Device Orchestration link, four newly available protected apps, and new Windows settings catalog policies. The supplied administrator guidance says these options can be evaluated and configured as relevant.

keyChanges.title: The Intune roadmap page removes six previously listed items
keyChanges.detail: The In development page date changed from January 7 to February 2, 2026, and six roadmap entries were removed. The removed entries include EPM support for AVD single-session VMs, Lenovo Device Orchestration integration, and several settings catalog, task, and assignment-filter updates. The page no longer provides those roadmap details; no configuration or migration is specified.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager guidance adds SQL 2022 and compatibility boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The page now lists SQL Server 2022 Express for secondary sites with Configuration Manager version 2509, states that SQL Server 2022 compatibility level 160 is unsupported, and marks SQL Server 2014 editions as deprecated. SQL Server 2014 support ended in July 2024, so administrators should review database compatibility before deployment and plan upgrades where applicable.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents Extended Protection from version 2409
keyChanges.detail: The SQL Server support guidance now states that Configuration Manager supports SQL Extended Protection for Authentication starting with version 2409. Administrators can use the capability to enhance security and reduce man-in-the-middle attack risk for SQL connections; no mandatory action is specified.

keyChanges.title: CMG authentication guidance clarifies Enhanced HTTP and HTTPS choices
keyChanges.detail: The updated authentication guidance explains that CMG-enabled management points can use Enhanced HTTP or HTTPS, and clarifies when PKI certificates must be exported and when HTTPS is needed. This gives administrators more targeted guidance when selecting management-point authentication and certificate handling.

2026-02-05.headline: EPM guidance for AVD single-session VMs leads Intune’s February update
2026-02-05.overview: The meaningful content changes are concentrated in Intune release, archive, and in-development guidance: EPM support for AVD single-session VMs, a Lenovo Device Orchestration admin-center link, four protected apps, new Windows Settings Catalog policies, and broader platform-management options. A separate What's New revision changed the displayed date from February 2 to January 12, 2026, and removed the Service release 2601 section and its entries, so release-history coverage now differs across the updated pages. The period is otherwise dominated by 115 Windows Autopilot updates, mostly metadata or formatting cleanup with no stated enrollment or configuration change.
2026-02-05.adminImpact: Administrators can use the Intune entries to plan EPM, protected-app, Settings Catalog, OEMConfig, device-cleanup, and macOS local-administrator workflows; the supplied records specify no required task or deadline. The In Development content is planning information, including the explicitly planned Lenovo Device Orchestration link. Autopilot's repeated metadata edits require no configuration action, while its known-issues page now marks an issue resolved in February 2026. Administrators relying on the What's New page for Service release 2601 information should note that one revision no longer displays those entries.

keyChanges.title: February guidance documents EPM for AVD single-session VMs
keyChanges.detail: The February 2, 2026 What's New update documents EPM support for AVD single-session VMs. The same entry lists a Lenovo Device Orchestration link in the admin center, four newly available protected apps, and new Windows Settings Catalog policies. No administrator action is stated.

keyChanges.title: The Intune archive records wider platform-management options
keyChanges.detail: The archive adds EPM wildcard matching, RugGear OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise, new iOS/iPadOS and macOS Settings Catalog settings, platform-specific device cleanup rules, and macOS ADE local-administrator configuration with Microsoft LAPS support. No task or deadline is specified.

keyChanges.title: In-development guidance expands filtering and offboarding scope
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page now lists Android management-mode filtering, expanded Android and iOS assignment-filter values, Device Offboarding Agent integration with admin tasks, new Apple Settings Catalog updates, EPM support for AVD single-session VMs, and a planned Lenovo Device Orchestration link.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot’s known-issues page marks an issue resolved
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device preparation known-issues page is dated February 5, 2026, and marks the issue resolved in February 2026. The supplied change specifies no remediation or deadline.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot reference pages receive broad metadata cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The representative Hybrid Azure AD Join Device Group edit removes the ms.collection and highpri metadata entries, matching the pattern across many Autopilot page updates. These changes are described as metadata or formatting edits and specify no enrollment-procedure or administrator-configuration change.

2026-02-06.headline: Apple configuration guides and Win32 silent-install limits headline Intune’s February 6 changes
2026-02-06.overview: New Apple guidance is the period’s clearest documentation expansion: separate articles now cover Wi-Fi, VPN, custom settings, device features, and device restrictions for iOS/iPadOS and macOS, with prerequisites and supported-scope details. More operationally, Intune guidance explicitly says Win32 installations must not require dialogs, prompts, UI input, or serviceui.exe workarounds, while the Remote Help endpoint list changes. The main Configuration Manager exception is a software update point warning about oversized synchronization selections and products or categories it cannot deploy; much of the remaining activity is link and wording consolidation.
2026-02-06.adminImpact: Apple administrators can use the new pages to plan and configure profiles; the custom-settings procedure covers importing Apple Configurator or Profile Manager exports, while the Wi-Fi, VPN, feature, and restriction pages expose platform and enrollment limits. Review Win32 packages for silent execution and update Remote Help firewall or proxy allowlists for the current endpoints. Software update point administrators should narrow synchronization to necessary products and categories; the In Development entries provide planning context only, with no action or deadline stated.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s In Development page adds several planning signals
keyChanges.detail: The page now lists EPM support for AVD single-session VMs, a planned Lenovo Device Orchestration link, new Apple and Android Settings Catalog options, Device Offboarding Agent admin-task integration, and expanded managed-app assignment filters. These entries support future planning, with no required action or deadline stated.

keyChanges.title: Apple Wi-Fi profiles gain a dedicated Intune configuration reference
keyChanges.detail: The new article covers iOS/iPadOS and macOS Wi-Fi profiles, including prerequisites, authentication, SSIDs, security types, proxy options, and iOS/iPadOS MAC address randomization. Administrators can use it when creating and deploying Apple Wi-Fi profiles.

keyChanges.title: Intune guidance states that Win32 installers must run without user interaction
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says Intune does not support interactive Win32 installations involving dialog boxes, prompts, UI input, or workarounds such as serviceui.exe. Review packages and commands to ensure installations run silently.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help endpoint guidance adds and replaces firewall destinations
keyChanges.detail: The Intune endpoints page adds `*.dm.microsoft.com` and replaces `*.trouter.skype.com` with `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft` in the Remote Help endpoint list. Review proxy and firewall allowlists to ensure the updated destinations are permitted.

keyChanges.title: Software update point guidance warns against broad synchronization selections
keyChanges.detail: The page says selecting too many products or categories can reduce performance because devices scan every update in the SUSDB. It also identifies Dynamic Updates, Servicing Drivers, legacy Office and operating systems, and several category types as content Configuration Manager can’t deploy; limit synchronization to relevant, necessary selections.

2026-02-07.headline: Remote Help troubleshooting now points administrators to Policy CSP for blocked notifications
2026-02-07.overview: The period’s sole change updates the Remote Help Troubleshoot Monitor guidance. When a device blocks applications from using notifications, the troubleshooting documentation now directs administrators to Policy CSP - Notifications for the relevant policy details.
2026-02-07.adminImpact: Use Policy CSP - Notifications when investigating Remote Help issues involving blocked application notifications.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help adds a Policy CSP - Notifications troubleshooting reference
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help troubleshooting documentation now directs administrators to Policy CSP - Notifications when applications are blocked from using notifications on a device.

2026-02-09.headline: Windows 11 25H2 becomes a selectable target for Intune readiness reports
2026-02-09.overview: The period’s clearest administrator-facing change is support for Windows 11, version 25H2 as a selectable target in Intune’s Windows feature update compatibility risks and device readiness reports. Windows Autopilot guidance adds version-specific fixes for deployment timeouts, while service release 2601 documents EPM support for AVD single-session VMs and related app and settings additions. Other updates tighten Managed Home Screen prerequisites and Win32 script-result troubleshooting; the remaining changes are mainly terminology, indexing, query, metadata, and roadmap-page edits.
2026-02-09.adminImpact: Select Windows 11, version 25H2 when assessing readiness and compatibility. For Windows Autopilot error 0x80004005 timeouts, verify the applicable Windows update: KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, or KB5070312 or later for 23H2. Grant Managed Home Screen the Alarms & Reminders permission before using the documented remote actions, and check Win32 script exit codes and output when detection remains not installed.

keyChanges.title: Intune readiness reports add Windows 11, version 25H2 as a target
keyChanges.detail: The Windows feature update compatibility risks and device readiness reports now support Windows 11, version 25H2 as a selectable target OS. Administrators can use it to assess device readiness and compatibility risks.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot records version-specific fixes for 0x80004005 deployment timeouts
keyChanges.detail: The Known Issues guidance documents deployment timeouts with error 0x80004005. The issue is resolved by KB5065789 or later for Windows 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, and KB5070312 or later for 23H2.

keyChanges.title: Service release 2601 documents EPM support for AVD single-session VMs
keyChanges.detail: The release guidance lists EPM support for AVD single-session VMs, a Lenovo Device Orchestration portal link, four newly available protected apps, and new Windows settings catalog policies. Administrators can use these options where applicable; no required configuration change is stated.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen Device Restore now requires Alarms & Reminders permission
keyChanges.detail: The Device Restore remote action requires Managed Home Screen to have the Alarms & Reminders permission granted before the action is run.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app guidance clarifies script output and failed detection handling
keyChanges.detail: The Intune agent evaluates script STDOUT, STDERR, and the exit code. A nonzero exit code indicates failure and leaves the detection status as not installed, giving administrators a more precise basis for troubleshooting installation results.

2026-02-10.headline: Intune will exclude long-inactive devices from reports starting in late February
2026-02-10.overview: The clearest service-level change is a planned reporting adjustment: beginning in late February 2026, devices inactive for 12 months or more will be excluded from Intune reports, which may reduce reported counts. The period also brought substantial Apple configuration-documentation changes, including new Wi-Fi, iCloud, and Kerberos guidance alongside the removal of ten standalone Apple reference pages, plus a Configuration Manager port correction.
2026-02-10.adminImpact: No immediate remediation is required for the Intune reporting change, but devices must check in to remain included. Apple administrators should account for the removed reference pages and use current related guidance for configuration workflows. Configuration Manager administrators reviewing firewall rules should use UDP 1434 for SQL Server Browser traffic.

keyChanges.title: Inactive devices will drop out of Intune reports in late February
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late February 2026, Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12 months or more from reports. Counts may decrease because reports will represent active devices; devices must check in to remain included, and the message states that no other action is required.

keyChanges.title: Standalone iOS custom-profile guidance was removed
