The former Windows Update for Business article was deleted, while Advanced Analytics Device Query guidance tightens documented role requirements and Intune corrects the Microsoft Graph hostname for China environments.
2026-09-02.adminImpact: Review devices using Windows Update client policies because affected updates may appear as Unknown, with documented limitations for compliance reporting, Microsoft app updates, third-party updates, and software-update-based client deployment. Check Device Query custom-role assignments, use https://graph.chinacloudapi.cn for China connections, and replace bookmarks or references to the deleted Windows Update for Business article.

keyChanges.title: Windows Update client policies gain expanded co-management guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new Configuration Manager article covers co-management scenarios, scan-source policies, common pitfalls, troubleshooting, and the effects of receiving Windows updates directly from Windows Update. It notes potential Unknown status for affected updates and limitations involving compliance reporting, Microsoft app updates, third-party updates, and software-update-based client deployment.

keyChanges.title: Former Windows Update for Business guidance was deleted
keyChanges.detail: The article covering Windows Update client policies, co-management considerations, limitations, prerequisites, and client-identification procedures was removed. Administrators relying on it should locate the current guidance and update saved references.

keyChanges.title: Multi-device Device Query roles now require managed-device access
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Analytics guidance now describes custom roles as needing permissions to view and access managed devices, giving Organization/Read and Managed devices/Read as examples. The separate Managed Devices/Query permission is no longer listed.

keyChanges.title: Device Query guidance now requires a custom role
keyChanges.detail: The Device Query article now specifies that users must be assigned a custom role and no longer lists Help Desk Operator as a role option. Review assignments for administrators who need to use Device Query.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s China endpoint list switches Microsoft Graph hostnames
keyChanges.detail: The China endpoints page now lists https://graph.chinacloudapi.cn instead of https://graph.chinacloudapi.us. Update configurations or connection references that still use the previous hostname.

2026-09-16.headline: Intune will move Windows 11 health attestation to Azure Attestation by early 2027
2026-09-16.overview: Microsoft’s Message Center announced a planned Intune migration from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation for Windows 11 devices. The change affects compliance evaluation for devices using health-based policies and introduces a network-access dependency on Azure Attestation endpoints.
2026-09-16.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to permit network access to the required Azure Attestation endpoints before the early 2027 migration. Without that access, Windows 11 devices using health-based policies may experience compliance-evaluation failures.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation is moving to Microsoft Azure Attestation
keyChanges.detail: Intune plans to migrate Windows Health Attestation from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation by early 2027. Windows 11 devices using health-based compliance policies could fail compliance evaluation if they cannot reach Azure Attestation endpoints.

2026-09-17.headline: Intune will shift Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation to Microsoft Azure Attestation
2026-09-17.overview: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice announces that Intune will migrate Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation from the current Device Health Attestation service to Microsoft Azure Attestation. The change is service-side and will occur automatically.
2026-09-17.adminImpact: The notice identifies no administrator procedure or customer-side action; administrators should understand this as an automatic Intune service migration.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation evaluation moves from DHA to MAA
keyChanges.detail: Intune will replace the current Device Health Attestation service with Microsoft Azure Attestation for Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation. Microsoft describes the migration as an automatic, service-side change.

2026-09-24.headline: Security Copilot joins E5/E7 while Autopatch adds granular update approvals
2026-09-24.overview: The period brings two substantive Message Center announcements: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5/E7 plans, while Windows Autopatch is rolling out more detailed control over update approvals and recovery management.
2026-09-24.adminImpact: Microsoft 365 E5/E7 organizations do not need to purchase or take action to receive Security Copilot, including monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools. Intune administrators can use the Autopatch enhancements to customize approvals, deferrals, and pauses for supported updates, with per-device reporting available as the rollout continues through October 15, 2026.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5/E7
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot is now part of Microsoft 365 E5/E7, with agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal. Included benefits are monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools; additional paid features remain available, and organizations can opt out through support.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch expands update approval and recovery controls
keyChanges.detail: Enhancements rolling out from September 1 through October 15, 2026 add customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferral settings, update pausing, and per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates.

2026-09-28.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 sets new SQL prerequisites and retires Asset Intelligence reporting
2026-09-28.overview: Configuration Manager 2609 is the clear story for this period. The version table records build 5.00.9152.1000 as released on 28 September 2026, with support through 28 March 2028, while the accompanying guidance establishes new SQL and ODBC gates, changes database-driver handling, removes Asset Intelligence surfaces, and narrows client support. The practical impact is concentrated in Configuration Manager infrastructure used alongside Intune.
2026-09-28.adminImpact: Before installing or updating to 2609, verify SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later, ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later, and the documented incompatible-driver exclusions; unsupported versions can block setup. Confirm that secondary sites meet the SQL Server 2017 Express CU2 requirement and update the Visual C++ Redistributable where required. Review procedures that depend on SQL Server Native Client, inventory Asset Intelligence reporting dependencies and affected Windows Server 2012-era clients, and apply the version-specific TRUSTWORTHY instruction: omit it for 2609 and later, but retain it for 2603 and earlier.

keyChanges.title: ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 and SQL Server 2017 CU2 become 2609 gates
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisite-check guidance requires ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later for 2609 and later, and SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later starting with 2609. Unsupported versions can block installation or upgrades, and the page identifies incompatible ODBC releases.

keyChanges.title: 2609 installs Microsoft OLE DB Driver and drops SQL Server Native Client
keyChanges.detail: Starting in 2609, Configuration Manager automatically installs the Microsoft OLE DB Driver for SQL Server and no longer requires SQL Server Native Client. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier retain the previous Native Client behavior.

keyChanges.title: Asset Intelligence home-page sections and reports are removed in 2609
keyChanges.detail: Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status are removed from the Asset Intelligence home page, along with Asset Intelligence reports. The earlier procedures apply only to 2603 and earlier; the updated page points administrators to the product lifecycle dashboard and Asset Intelligence client settings.

keyChanges.title: TRUSTWORTHY is no longer required for 2609 SQLCLR loading
keyChanges.detail: For 2609 and later, TRUSTWORTHY isn't needed to load Microsoft-signed SQLCLR assemblies, including databases using SQL Server Always On availability groups. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier still require TRUSTWORTHY to be enabled.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server 2012 family leaves the 2609 client-support matrix
keyChanges.detail: Starting with Configuration Manager 2609, Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, and their Windows Storage Server editions are no longer supported as client operating systems.

2026-09-29.headline: VPP token reuse can erase available assignments, Intune guidance warns
2026-09-29.overview: The period is dominated by documentation consolidation, but several updates have direct operational value. Apple guidance now warns about losing available app assignments when an existing VPP token is re-uploaded for DDM, and clarifies that app configuration policies support MDM-managed apps only. New Intune guidance also documents device renaming, editable device properties, and inventory collection timing. Most other edits correct URLs or reflect the current device-overview action paths, such as Remove data > Retire and Secure > Rotate FileVault recovery key.
2026-09-29.adminImpact: Review Apple Business and Intune app-management procedures before changing token or app-management models. For device administration, use the new rename and Properties guidance, exclude hybrid-joined Windows devices from rename plans, and allow up to 24 hours for initial inventory collection. Follow the revised menu paths when performing documented device actions.

keyChanges.title: VPP guidance warns against re-uploading tokens for DDM
keyChanges.detail: The Manage VPP for Apple guidance says re-uploading an existing VPP token for DDM causes available app assignments to be lost. It recommends creating a new Apple Business token for DDM, while using MDM for available assignments and apps that require app configuration policies. Administrators should not re-upload tokens that already have available assignments.

keyChanges.title: iOS and iPadOS app configuration is documented as MDM-only
keyChanges.detail: The managed iOS guidance now states that app configuration policies support only MDM-managed apps and cannot configure DDM apps. The setup procedure was also renumbered, so DDM apps requiring this configuration path need a different management approach.

keyChanges.title: New guidance documents device renaming rules and limitations
keyChanges.detail: The new rename-device article covers renaming managed devices from the Intune admin center, supported platforms, platform-specific naming rules, and bulk-renaming variables. It explicitly documents that hybrid-joined Windows devices aren't supported, which should be accounted for when standardizing inventory names.

keyChanges.title: New Properties guidance covers editable device metadata
keyChanges.detail: A new article explains how to edit a managed device's name, ownership, primary user, notes, and scope tags from the Properties tab. Scope-tag changes affect device visibility for delegated administrators, while the primary-user workflow is now documented alongside the other editable properties.

keyChanges.title: Inventory guidance sets a 24-hour initial collection window
keyChanges.detail: The Collect device properties guidance now says active devices collect inventory multiple times per day, while initial collection can take up to 24 hours because full synchronization runs once daily. Administrators should allow that window before treating missing initial inventory as a problem.

2026-09-30.headline: Intune iOS enrollment requires the deprecated computer-sync setting set to No
2026-09-30.overview: The period contains five updated pages and no new or removed items. The most consequential Intune change is enrollment guidance requiring Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication to be set to No; the page says Apple deprecated Sync with computers in iOS 13 and that it is no longer included in enrollment policies. Other updates clarify Managed Google Play onboarding scope, macOS PKG retry behavior, and Managed Home Screen terminology, while a Configuration Manager matrix adds Windows 11 26H2 support indicators.
2026-09-30.adminImpact: Set Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication to No in applicable iOS enrollment policies. For other changes, account for required app installation on dedicated devices and up to three retries for failed macOS app installations while the app remains assigned. Use the updated Configuration Manager matrix when evaluating Windows 11 26H2 support.

keyChanges.title: iOS enrollment setting is marked for removal
keyChanges.detail: The updated Setup Automated iOS guidance says Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication must be set to No. It also records that Apple deprecated Sync with computers in iOS 13 and that the setting is no longer included in enrollment policies; administrators should apply No in applicable policies.

keyChanges.title: macOS PKG guidance documents repeated installation retries
keyChanges.detail: Failed macOS app installations are retried at the next agent check-in, with up to three retries while the app remains assigned. Administrators should account for these attempts when monitoring deployment failures.

keyChanges.title: Managed Google Play onboarding guidance includes dedicated devices
keyChanges.detail: During onboarding, Intune, Microsoft Authenticator, and Company Portal are installed as required apps on dedicated devices, in addition to fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. Dedicated-device administrators should expect these installations, which support Conditional Access.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager matrix lists Windows 11 26H2
keyChanges.detail: The Support for Windows 11 matrix now lists Windows 11 version 26H2, build 10.0.26300, with support indicators shown as ❌, ✅, and ✅. Administrators can use the revised matrix when evaluating 26H2 support.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen setting now uses the full product name
keyChanges.detail: The app-exclusion setting description spells out Managed Home Screen instead of using MHS when referring to authentication, making the applicable setting easier to identify.

2026-10-01.headline: Apple OS 27 inventory and MEFERI OEMConfig join Intune’s planned changes
2026-10-01.overview: Intune’s updated In Development page now lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data, MEFERI OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise, removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads, and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. A separate Managed Home Screen update revises wording around excluding apps from the silence setting and changes authoring metadata.
2026-10-01.adminImpact: Administrators should track the planned inventory, OEMConfig, Apple software-update, and Windows Account Protection changes; no action or deadline is stated. The Managed Home Screen wording update indicates no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Apple OS 27 and MEFERI support appear on the development roadmap
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page now lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data and MEFERI OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise. It also identifies removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen updates the silence-setting exclusion guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Configure Managed Home Screen page revises the description for excluding apps from the silence setting and changes its authoring metadata. No administrator action is indicated.

2026-10-02.headline: EPM system-settings policy covers controlled IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes
2026-10-02.overview: The period’s most consequential update centers on Endpoint Privilege Management’s Elevation system settings policy, which documents how standard Windows users can make selected network changes under administrator-defined controls. Intune guidance also tightens Android reset and factory reset protection expectations, while Advanced Analytics documents unavailable device identifiers.
2026-10-02.adminImpact: EPM administrators can delegate IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes while requiring confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both; an EPM elevation settings policy must be enabled. Android administrators should review Factory reset protection emails configuration and Android 15 post-reset account re-entry requirements. Analytics consumers should account for unavailable ICCID and SimInfo data in the documented device populations.

keyChanges.title: EPM documents controlled network-setting delegation
keyChanges.detail: A new Endpoint Privilege Management page describes policies that let standard Windows users change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS settings. Administrators can require confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both, and devices need an EPM elevation settings policy enabled.

keyChanges.title: Android reset guidance links FRP enforcement to email configuration
keyChanges.detail: The Corporate Methods guidance states that Settings resets don’t enforce factory reset protection when Factory reset protection emails is Not configured. For Android 15 devices with a configured Google account email, the account must be re-entered after the reset.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics records ICCID and SimInfo data limitations
keyChanges.detail: The schema reference now states that ICCID isn’t supported on Windows. It also continues to specify that SimInfo isn’t supported for Android Enterprise personally owned devices with a work profile.

2026-10-06.headline: Windows 11 26H2 baseline settings and GCCH Remote Help guidance lead Intune updates
2026-10-06.overview: Intune’s most consequential update documents the Windows 11 version 26H2 security baseline, including Settings Catalog support, new settings, updated defaults, and revised guidance. Existing baseline profiles do not update automatically. The period also records Remote Help availability in US Government Community Cloud High for Android and Windows, clarifies Defender for Endpoint connector behavior on Android COBO and COPE devices, and previews a November 2026 Purview DLP and Intune approval workflow improvement. Configuration Manager 2609 guidance records a significant Windows Server client-support cutoff.
2026-10-06.adminImpact: Review existing security baseline profiles before adopting the 26H2 baseline; create a new profile or update an existing one because profiles do not update automatically. When configuring the Defender for Endpoint connector for Android COBO or COPE, enable Grant MTD role permissions. GCCH support teams can use Remote Help for enrolled Android and Windows devices with role-based access and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in. Purview and Intune administrators can prepare for the November 2026 setup and approval workflow changes without changing existing policies or enforcement. Configuration Manager administrators planning version 2609 should identify Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, and Storage Server clients and upgrade them to a supported Windows Server version.

keyChanges.title: 26H2 security baseline guidance requires explicit profile action
keyChanges.detail: Intune now documents the Windows 11 version 26H2 security baseline and Settings Catalog support, including new settings, updated defaults, and revised guidance. Existing security baseline profiles do not update automatically; administrators adopting 26H2 must create a new profile or update an existing one.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint setup documents Android COBO and COPE behavior
keyChanges.detail: The connector guidance states that enabling the Defender for Endpoint toggle automatically launches the app during setup on Android COBO and COPE devices. Grant MTD role permissions must also be enabled.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help is available in GCCH for Android and Windows
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance now states that Remote Help is available in US Government Community Cloud High environments for Android and Windows devices, enabling GCCH IT support staff to provide real-time troubleshooting with role-based access controls and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP will add Intune multi-admin approval for Edge unmanaged apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting November 2026, Microsoft Purview DLP will improve setup and support Intune multi-admin approval for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business, with clearer status, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators. Existing policies and enforcement will not change.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 drops legacy Windows Server client support
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager version 2609 no longer supports Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, or their Windows Storage Server editions as client operating systems. Affected devices must be moved to a supported Windows Server version.

2026-10-07.headline: Endpoint guidance adds a global trouter communications hostname
2026-10-07.overview: Intune’s Endpoints guidance now lists `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft` for all regions and removes the separate `go-amer`, `go-eu`, and `go-apac` entries.
2026-10-07.adminImpact: Administrators maintaining network allowlists should review and update them against the revised endpoint table, including the new all-regions hostname and the removed regional entries.

keyChanges.title: Endpoints table consolidates regional entries
keyChanges.detail: The endpoint table adds `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft` for all regions and removes the separate `go-amer`, `go-eu`, and `go-apac` entries. Review allowlist configurations that rely on the endpoint guidance.

2026-10-08.headline: Intune guidance sees broad author-metadata reassignment across compliance, security, and enrollment
2026-10-08.overview: This was a maintenance-heavy period: all 42 recorded items were updates, including 40 for Intune and one each for Endpoint Privilege Management and Windows Autopilot. The supplied changes primarily revise page authors, `ms.author` values, and—in one Intune case—two DevRel ontology links. The evidence does not identify changes to Intune settings, features, availability, or device behavior.
2026-10-08.adminImpact: No administrator action is required for the documented changes. They affect documentation ownership and links rather than policies, configurations, or deployed capabilities.

keyChanges.title: Compliance guidance changes author ownership metadata
keyChanges.detail: The `Deploy Compliance Step 3` page changes its author and `ms.author` metadata from `lenewsad` to `paolomatarazzo`. No administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Email protection guidance updates DevRel ontology links
keyChanges.detail: `Protect Email Unmanaged Devices` updates its page author metadata and two DevRel ontology links. No administrator action is specified.

keyChanges.title: EPM Admin Tasks changes the Microsoft author alias
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Privilege Management `Admin Tasks` article changes its `ms.author` value from `lanewsad` to `paoloma`. No administrator action is indicated.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot cloud-native tutorial changes page attribution
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot `Tutorial Cloud Native Setup` page changes its author metadata from Scott Breen to Paolo Marotta. No administrator action is required.

2026-10-09.headline: Samsung Knox E-FOTA guidance now names public cloud and GCC High
2026-10-09.overview: The period brought three Intune documentation updates focused on government-cloud coverage. The Government Service article now says advanced capabilities support GCC High and/or DoD, with availability varying by cloud and detailed in linked documentation. Two Samsung Knox E-FOTA articles now identify support in the public cloud and GCC High.
2026-10-09.adminImpact: Administrators working in GCC High or DoD should check the linked capability documentation for cloud-specific availability. Samsung device administrators in GCC High can use the updated E-FOTA management and setup guidance; the evidence specifies no additional required action.

keyChanges.title: Government Service guidance identifies GCC High and DoD coverage
keyChanges.detail: The article now states that advanced capabilities support GCC High and/or DoD and directs administrators to linked documentation for cloud-specific availability.

keyChanges.title: Manage FOTA guidance names public-cloud and GCC High support
keyChanges.detail: The Manage Fota article now states that Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration is supported in the public cloud and U.S. Government Community Cloud (GCC) High.

keyChanges.title: Samsung Knox setup guidance adds GCC High coverage
keyChanges.detail: The setup guidance now states that Samsung Knox E-FOTA updates are supported in the public cloud and GCC High, giving administrators a reference for configuring updates in GCC High.

2026-10-10.headline: Remote Help planning guidance now flags unattended sign-in limits in Switzerland North
2026-10-10.overview: Remote Help’s planning guidance now states that tenants in the Switzerland North datacenter region cannot use Windows unattended remote sign-in. The update is a regional planning limitation for administrators using the capability.
2026-10-10.adminImpact: Administrators with tenants in Switzerland North should account for the limitation when planning Remote Help usage. No action is required because of the documentation update itself.

keyChanges.title: Switzerland North tenants cannot use Windows unattended remote sign-in
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help Plan documentation now states that tenants in the Switzerland North datacenter region cannot use Windows unattended remote sign-in. Administrators should consider this limitation when planning Remote Help deployments in that region.

2026-10-12.headline: Managed Google Play guidance specifies a 3,000-app per-device targeting limit
2026-10-12.overview: The Add Managed Google Play guidance now states that policies support up to 3,000 targeted apps per device for specified Android Enterprise corporate-owned and personally owned work profile scenarios.
2026-10-12.adminImpact: Administrators should account for the 3,000-app limit when targeting apps to affected Android Enterprise devices. No administrator action is explicitly required.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise app-targeting limit is documented
keyChanges.detail: The Intune app-management guidance specifies a maximum of 3,000 targeted apps per device for the covered corporate-owned and personally owned work profile scenarios.

2026-10-13.headline: 60-day AVD retention threshold, 12-hour macOS sync, and Remote Help 5.2.1210.0 lead updates
2026-10-13.overview: This was a detail-focused period for Intune. The What's New index lists Windows Remote Help 5.2.1210.0 with stability and observability improvements; Azure Virtual Desktop multi-session guidance specifies a 60-day inactivity threshold for permanent device-record deletion; and macOS token guidance specifies automatic synchronization every 12 hours. Apple enrollment terminology and Configuration Manager deprecation entries were also refreshed.
2026-10-13.adminImpact: Use the 60-day inactivity threshold when planning Azure Virtual Desktop multi-session record retention and review the listed Remote Help version for Windows deployments. The macOS guidance requires no administrator action: manual sync limits and completion behavior are unchanged. Apple enrollment planners can use the licensing entry to identify enrollment without user affinity or Entra Shared Device Mode. Configuration Manager administrators using the Exchange Server connector should account for its documented retirement timeline.

keyChanges.title: Windows Remote Help entry names version 5.2.1210.0
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's New index now lists Remote Help for Windows version 5.2.1210.0 and describes stability and observability improvements. Administrators can review the version for Windows deployments.

keyChanges.title: AVD multi-session guidance specifies a 60-day inactivity threshold
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now states that Intune attempts to permanently delete device records inactive for 60 days or more. This threshold is separate from administrator-configured cleanup rules and should be included in orphaned-device retention planning.

keyChanges.title: macOS token guidance specifies 12-hour automatic synchronization
keyChanges.detail: The automatic sync interval is now specified as every 12 hours instead of every 24 hours. Manual sync limits and completion behavior remain unchanged, and no administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Apple enrollment licensing guidance adds shared-device scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The Apple Device Enrollment Program entry now also references enrollment without user affinity or Entra Shared Device Mode, helping administrators identify the relevant enrollment scenario.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager entry records the Exchange connector’s deprecation timeline
keyChanges.detail: The entry lists the Exchange Server connector as deprecated, dated November 2021, with removal in the first release after November 1, 2022. Administrators using the connector should account for this documented retirement timeline.

2026-10-14.headline: CMG migration quota checks, ADK compatibility, CVE references, and macOS PSSO warnings lead updates
2026-10-14.overview: Configuration Manager 2609 guidance now adds a CMG VM scale set migration preflight: identify CMGs, calculate required vCPUs, check standard Dadv6 Family and regional quotas, and request increases where necessary because insufficient quota can trigger QuotaExceeded. The ADK support matrix points administrators to the 10.1.26100.x family, while two update entries identify addressed elevation-of-privilege vulnerabilities by CVE. Intune's macOS enrollment guidance also warns against assigning registration-enabling PSSO profiles to userless ADE devices.
2026-10-14.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators preparing an upgrade should verify quota availability for every CMG subscription and region before migration. Use the updated ADK compatibility guidance when selecting Windows PE media, and use the two CVE references to assess the security relevance of the associated updates. Intune administrators should review PSSO profile assignments and remove registration-enabling targeting from userless ADE devices to avoid unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected affinity.

keyChanges.title: CMG migration guidance adds a quota preflight
keyChanges.detail: Before upgrading, administrators are directed to identify CMGs, calculate required vCPUs, check standard Dadv6 Family and regional quotas, and request quota increases. Insufficient quota can cause a QuotaExceeded error during migration.

keyChanges.title: ADK guidance names 10.1.26100.9457 and redirects Windows PE planning
keyChanges.detail: The support matrix lists ADK 10.1.26100.9457 as the current September 2026 release and explains that 10.1.26100.x releases share Windows PE binaries. Known Windows PE issues for ADK 10.1.25398.1 are grouped separately, with administrators directed to the 10.1.26100.x family.

keyChanges.title: Update 38982839 now identifies CVE-2026-88075
keyChanges.detail: The update entry now states that 38982839 addresses the elevation-of-privilege vulnerability described in CVE-2026-88075, giving administrators a specific reference for assessing the update's security relevance.

keyChanges.title: Message Processing Engine guidance names CVE-2026-70049
keyChanges.detail: The issue entry now states that the update addresses the elevation-of-privilege vulnerability described in CVE-2026-70049, allowing administrators to map the hotfix to its documented security issue.

keyChanges.title: macOS PSSO assignments gain a userless ADE enrollment warning
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance warns that targeting userless ADE devices with PSSO profiles that enable registration during Setup Assistant can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected affinity.

2026-10-15.headline: Windows MDM-only enrollment loses CNAME auto-discovery support January 15, 2027
2026-10-15.overview: The period’s consequential change is Intune’s planned retirement of DNS CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment on January 15, 2027. A separate partner-directory update expands setup links and adds Fleet, Iru, and Samsung Knox Manage (Compliance).
2026-10-15.adminImpact: Organizations using Windows MDM-only enrollment with CNAME auto-discovery should update enrollment procedures so users manually enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL before January 15, 2027. Existing devices and other enrollment methods are unaffected. The partner-directory update requires no action but gives administrators more direct integration guidance.

keyChanges.title: CNAME auto-discovery ending for Windows MDM-only enrollment
keyChanges.detail: Starting January 15, 2027, Intune will no longer support DNS CNAME auto-discovery in Windows MDM-only enrollment. Users in affected organizations will need to manually enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL; existing devices and other enrollment methods remain unaffected.

keyChanges.title: Third-party partner directory adds integrations and setup links
keyChanges.detail: The Third Party Partners page now links existing partner entries to setup documentation and adds Fleet, Iru, and Samsung Knox Manage (Compliance). The Citrix entry was renamed and linked to its documentation.

2026-10-17.headline: Windows elevation defaults remain device-scoped despite user-group assignments
2026-10-17.overview: Three Endpoint Privilege Management guidance updates consistently state that Windows elevation settings policies and their default elevation responses apply at device scope, even when assigned to groups containing users. A separate Samsung Knox E-FOTA update documents a one-account-per-tenant limit and region matching requirement.
2026-10-17.adminImpact: For Endpoint Privilege Management, do not use different user-group policy assignments to create per-user default elevation responses; use user-group elevation rules for user-specific application behavior while keeping the device-wide default consistent. For Samsung Knox E-FOTA, verify that the connected account and region match device registration and plan around one connected account per Intune tenant.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management defaults apply to the whole device
keyChanges.detail: Windows elevation settings policy client settings remain device-scoped. The default elevation response applies to all users on the device, and assigning the policy to a user group does not make that default per-user.

keyChanges.title: Samsung Knox E-FOTA requires one matching account and region
keyChanges.detail: An Intune tenant supports only one connected Samsung Knox E-FOTA account. The account and region must match where devices are registered; otherwise, device registration can fail even when the connector reports Connected.

2026-10-19.headline: macOS lockout-timer setup and Tunnel encryption guidance lead Intune updates
2026-10-19.overview: The period was led by two actionable Intune guidance changes: a prerequisite for managing macOS lockout timers and stronger encryption-at-rest guidance for Microsoft Tunnel container files. Other updates standardized Samsung partner-link terminology, while a Security Copilot Message Center notice was corrected and should be disregarded.
2026-10-19.adminImpact: For macOS password management, configure Failed Attempts Reset In Minutes in the Settings catalog before rotating the password if you need to manage the lockout timer. For Microsoft Tunnel containers, review Docker or Podman encryption options and consider enabling encryption at rest. No action is required for the Samsung link-label update, and recipients can disregard MC1478465.

keyChanges.title: macOS setup now identifies the lockout-timer prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The setup guidance directs administrators to configure Failed Attempts Reset In Minutes in the Settings catalog before rotating the password when they need to manage the lockout timer.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel guidance recommends encryption at rest for container files
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisites page states that encryption at rest is optional but strongly recommended for files used by Microsoft Tunnel containers, with links to Linux distribution and container-platform guidance.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot E5/E7 inclusion notice was marked for disregard
keyChanges.detail: The updated Message Center notice says it did not reach its intended audience and tells recipients they can safely disregard it, apologizing for the confusion.

keyChanges.title: Samsung partner-link terminology now uses “Samsung Knox Manage”
keyChanges.detail: The third-party partners page changed the link label from “Samsung Knox Manage (Compliance)” to “Samsung Knox Manage”; the destination URL is unchanged.

2026-10-21.headline: Intune expands Sync to iOS/iPadOS while Autopilot details MDM-provider onboarding
2026-10-21.overview: Intune’s comprehensive Sync device action now covers Windows and iOS/iPadOS, including configuration policies, apps, and scripts. A new Windows Autopilot article defines the limited-access request and technical onboarding path for MDM providers. Other notable updates specify CMPivot certificate-trust requirements, revise the protected-app reference list, and tie a Configuration Manager 2603 fix to update rollup KB 39169655.
2026-10-21.adminImpact: Use Sync in the Intune admin center to initiate broader synchronization for iOS/iPadOS devices. Individual administrators have no onboarding action for the Windows Autopilot process, which targets MDM providers. If PowerShell uses AllSigned, verify trust for the Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011 certificate: Configuration Manager 2603 with its update rollup and version 2609 or later add it automatically, while earlier versions require manual export and trust. Review protected-app planning and use the 2603 rollup instead of a separate 37942646 hotfix where applicable.

keyChanges.title: Sync now covers iOS/iPadOS workloads
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s comprehensive Sync device action now applies to Windows and iOS/iPadOS and synchronizes key workloads such as configuration policies, apps, and scripts.

keyChanges.title: CMPivot trust handling is version-specific
keyChanges.detail: CMPivot is signed with the Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011 certificate. Configuration Manager 2603 with the update rollup and version 2609 or later automatically add the certificate to Trusted Publishers; earlier versions require manual certificate export.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot documents an MDM-provider integration path
keyChanges.detail: New guidance explains how MDM providers can request limited access to integrate their services with Windows Autopilot device association, covering prerequisites, request details, review, and technical onboarding.

keyChanges.title: Protected Apps reference removes two Android and iOS entries
keyChanges.detail: The reference list removes Microsoft Azure Information Protection Viewer and Microsoft Power Automate entries for Android and iOS, and updates the Fuze Mobile for Intune entry and related links.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 rollup absorbs a documented fix
keyChanges.detail: The 37942646 entry now states that the update is included in Configuration Manager 2603 update rollup KB 39169655, so a separate out-of-band hotfix isn’t required after the rollup is installed.

2026-10-22.headline: PowerShell sample guidance now points to the mggraph-intune-samples repository
2026-10-22.overview: The period is documentation maintenance centered on reference destinations. Intune setup, Graph API, and app-management guidance now points to microsoft/mggraph-intune-samples; Apple DDM app-settings guidance moves from the seed_OS_27_0 schema branch to the release branch; and iOS/iPadOS example pages use updated references. Configuration Manager TLS pages retain hotfix IDs 3099842 and 3099844 but remove their direct links.
2026-10-22.adminImpact: Use microsoft/mggraph-intune-samples when downloading Intune PowerShell samples or importing related policy templates. Administrators following the Configuration Manager TLS guidance must locate the support pages manually using hotfix IDs 3099842 and 3099844. The other reference-link updates do not call for configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: PowerShell sample links converge on the mggraph-intune-samples repository
keyChanges.detail: Setup Migration now links to microsoft/mggraph-intune-samples instead of microsoftgraph/powershell-intune-samples. Configure Graph API Access and Data Protection Framework guidance also directs administrators to that repository for Intune PowerShell examples and scripts.

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM app-settings schema guidance switches to the release branch
keyChanges.detail: The Apple DDM App Settings page changes its app.settings source-schema link from the seed_OS_27_0 branch to the release branch, directing administrators to the release schema reference.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager TLS pages retain hotfix IDs but remove direct links
keyChanges.detail: Enable TLS 1.2 Client now lists rollups 3099842 and 3099844 as plain text for Windows 8.1, Windows Server 2012 R2, and Windows Server 2012. Administrators must locate the applicable support references manually.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS supervised examples receive refreshed reference links
keyChanges.detail: The Supervised page changes the reference links used in its examples guidance. The guidance on evaluating threat environment, risk appetite, and usability remains unchanged; use the updated links when validating configurations.

2026-10-23.headline: New Intune device page becomes default in release 2609 with updated permissions
2026-10-23.overview: The period's main operational notice is the planned replacement of Intune's legacy device page with the new experience starting with the September (2609) release. The remaining updates document Apple VPP unlimited-license assignments and revise macOS troubleshooting guidance, including the documented check-in cadence and agent check-in procedure.
2026-10-23.adminImpact: Prepare administrators for the new device page, update internal documentation, and review the required Managed devices/Update permission plus the specific permissions for device actions. For Apple VPP deployments, unlimited-license assignments remove the need to manage license quantities. Use the revised macOS check-in cadence when troubleshooting, and note that the macOS management-agent article no longer documents the Terminal command for forcing a check-in.

keyChanges.title: New device page replaces the legacy default in release 2609
keyChanges.detail: The Intune device page experience is scheduled to become the default starting with the September (2609) release. Device-management features remain available, but administrators need the Managed devices/Update permission and the relevant action permissions. Microsoft advises updating documentation and reviewing permissions.

keyChanges.title: Apple VPP apps gain documented unlimited-license assignment support
keyChanges.detail: The Intune index now records that Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager VPP apps can be assigned with unlimited licenses on iOS/iPadOS, enabling deployment across an organization without managing license quantities.

keyChanges.title: macOS profile troubleshooting now uses a three-stage check-in cadence
keyChanges.detail: The documented macOS schedule is every 3 minutes for 15 minutes, every 15 minutes for 2 hours, and then about hourly. Administrators can use this cadence when waiting for or troubleshooting device-profile changes; no configuration change is stated.

keyChanges.title: macOS agent guidance removes the Terminal restart command
keyChanges.detail: The Management Agent for macOS article no longer includes the Terminal command to terminate and restart the IntuneMdmAgent process to initiate an Intune check-in. Administrators will not find that command-based method in the documented procedure.

2026-10-26.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers as CMG tiers adopt new VM sizes
2026-10-26.overview: Configuration Manager 2609 became globally available on October 26, 2026, while CMG guidance specifies new D2ads_v6, D4ads_v6, and D8ads_v6 sizes for the Small, Medium, and Large tiers. Intune updates add concrete guidance for AOSP referenced-app assignments and Apple device-wide VPN route enforcement.
2026-10-26.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators can install 2609 without the documented early-update-ring opt-in. Before upgrading CMG deployments, verify Azure-region availability for the new sizes and ensure Dadv6 Family and regional vCPU quotas have sufficient headroom. Intune administrators managing AOSP apps should account for package-name and assignment limitations, while Apple VPN administrators should use the documented Include all networks and Exclude local networks settings for device-wide profiles.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 is globally available
keyChanges.detail: The installation checklist now states that version 2609 became globally available on October 26, 2026, replacing the early-update-ring opt-in instructions. Administrators can install the update without that opt-in process.

keyChanges.title: CMG tiers adopt new VM sizes for 2609 and patched 2603
keyChanges.detail: For Configuration Manager 2609 and Configuration Manager 2603 with KB39169655, the Small, Medium, and Large CMG tiers use D2ads_v6, D4ads_v6, and D8ads_v6 respectively. Existing deployments migrate automatically to the corresponding tiers, while earlier versions retain the previous sizes.

keyChanges.title: AOSP referenced-app guidance defines assignment behavior
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance explains how to add AOSP referenced apps without an APK or Google Play selection. Required assignments unhide apps already resident on devices, Uninstall assignments hide them, and Available assignments aren't supported. The package name is required and can't be changed after the app is created.

keyChanges.title: Apple VPN profiles gain documented Enforce Routes configuration
keyChanges.detail: For device-wide VPN profiles on iOS/iPadOS and macOS, administrators configure Include all networks and Exclude local networks; Intune derives the Apple Enforce Routes value automatically. The settings don't apply to per-app VPN, and split tunneling isn't recommended with them.

2026-10-27.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 reaches all customers alongside CMG NAT and image changes
2026-10-27.overview: Configuration Manager version 2609 became globally available on October 26, allowing all customers to install it without using the early update ring. A separate 2603 update rollup adds security and functional fixes and documents CMG migration to a supported Windows Server 2022 image, Azure Load Balancer inbound NAT rules version 2, and newer VM sizes. Advanced Analytics also expanded its schema reference with Apple accessibility and content-cache fields.
2026-10-27.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators can install version 2609 directly. For the 2603 rollup, check Azure capacity and vCPU quotas before installation, upgrade the Configuration Manager console afterward, and install before September 30, 2027, to avoid the inbound NAT rules version 1 retirement. Advanced Analytics users can use the newly documented Apple fields to interpret accessibility and content-cache data.

keyChanges.title: Version 2609 is globally available
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now states that, as of October 26, 2026, Configuration Manager version 2609 is available for all customers to install without relying on the early update ring.

keyChanges.title: KB39169655 updates CMG migration and Azure infrastructure guidance
keyChanges.detail: The version 2603 update rollup documents security and functional fixes, CMG migrations to a supported Windows Server 2022 image, Azure Load Balancer inbound NAT rules version 2, and newer VM sizes. Administrators should check Azure capacity and vCPU quotas before installation, upgrade the console afterward, and install before September 30, 2027, to avoid the inbound NAT rules version 1 retirement.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics schema adds Apple accessibility and content-cache properties
keyChanges.detail: The Ref Data Platform Schema now documents AppleAccessibility properties for supervised iOS/iPadOS 16 or later devices, plus AppleContentCache, AppleContentCacheParent, and AppleContentCachePeer properties for macOS 27 or later.

2026-10-28.headline: Intune supports 100-device eSIM activation as EPM Network settings roll out
2026-10-28.overview: The period’s meaningful updates cover two distinct administrator concerns: Intune’s documented bulk eSIM workflow for newer corporate-owned Android devices, and Endpoint Privilege Management’s gradually available Network settings capability.
2026-10-28.adminImpact: Administrators can use a carrier activation server URL to activate eSIMs on up to 100 selected corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices running Android 15 or later. Bulk wipe retains eSIM plans by default, with an option to remove them. EPM administrators may not yet see Network settings in every tenant.

keyChanges.title: Bulk eSIM activation and wipe behavior documented for Android Enterprise
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune index states that administrators can activate eSIMs on up to 100 selected corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices running Android 15 or later through a carrier activation server URL. Bulk wipe preserves eSIM plans by default, while administrators can choose to remove them.

keyChanges.title: EPM Network settings identified as a gradual rollout
keyChanges.detail: The Manage System Settings guidance now says EPM System settings (Network settings) is rolling out gradually and may not be available in some tenants. The page also adds two supporting ontology links; no administrator action is required while availability catches up.

2026-10-29.headline: Windows PE BitLocker guidance drops Windows 7 steps for supported ADK and client versions
2026-10-29.overview: Configuration Manager’s “Preprovision BitLocker in Windows PE” guidance replaces Windows 7-specific instructions with general Windows guidance. It updates the boot image requirement to a supported ADK and Configuration Manager client version, and clarifies when to restart in Windows PE.
2026-10-29.adminImpact: Review affected task sequences and verify that their boot images use a supported ADK and updated Configuration Manager client version.

keyChanges.title: BitLocker preprovisioning guidance updates Windows PE requirements
keyChanges.detail: The article replaces Windows 7-specific steps with Windows guidance, updates the boot image requirement to a supported ADK and Configuration Manager client version, and clarifies when to restart in Windows PE.

2026-10-30.headline: iOS 27 shifts software updates to DDM as Intune ends legacy ADE authentication
2026-10-30.overview: The meaningful Intune changes center on retiring legacy Apple enrollment and update controls, alongside tighter Windows deployment options. Apple’s OS 27 guidance moves administrators to Declarative Device Management (DDM) for software updates, while the October 2026 (2610) release ends Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication for ADE with user affinity. Windows Autopilot guidance adds Enterprise App Management app gating and sets a processing cutoff for older Active Directory connectors. Most of the period’s 3,079 updates were mechanical metadata or link changes, particularly in Configuration Manager.
2026-10-30.adminImpact: Review iOS/iPadOS update policies and ADE profiles, especially any legacy MDM or UTC-based scheduling dependencies. Upgrade Intune Connector for Active Directory versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 because they can no longer process enrollment requests. App gating and Defender Safe Deployment are available as planning options; no mandatory configuration change is stated for those items, and existing legacy ADE profiles update automatically.

keyChanges.title: Apple moves iOS/iPadOS software-update controls to DDM
keyChanges.detail: The planning guidance states that Apple deprecated MDM-based software-update workloads and removed related commands with OS 27. It directs administrators to Software Update enforcement and Software Update Settings, with enforcement based on each device’s local time zone.

keyChanges.title: Intune ends Setup Assistant legacy authentication for ADE user affinity
keyChanges.detail: Support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication for Automated Device Enrollment with user affinity ended in the October 2026 (2610) service release. Existing profiles are automatically updated to modern authentication, and the legacy option is no longer available.

keyChanges.title: Older Intune AD connectors can no longer process Autopilot enrollments
keyChanges.detail: Intune Connector for Active Directory versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 are deprecated and can no longer process enrollment requests. Connector version 6.2504.2001.8 uses WebView2, removing the documented need to disable Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration on Windows Server.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation can gate setup on Enterprise App Management apps
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot device preparation policies can select Microsoft Intune Enterprise App Management auto-update apps and block setup until those apps are installed, allowing selected required applications to be present before users reach the desktop.

keyChanges.title: In-development guidance details a Defender Safe Deployment template
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s in-development guidance describes a dedicated template for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint safe deployment settings on Windows, including separate update channels for platform, engine, and security intelligence updates.

2026-11-02.headline: Configuration Manager TLS 1.2 guidance separates client tasks and sharpens .NET steps
2026-11-02.overview: All six updates affected Configuration Manager documentation. The most substantive revisions tighten TLS 1.2 client and server instructions, clarify that Cloud Management Gateway and co-management are independent but can be used together, and state that the console is always installed on every site server. The period also included tooling wording updates and removal of the Download MDT link from the index.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Administrators should use the revised TLS pages when reviewing .NET, registry, protocol, security-update, and architecture-specific guidance. The co-management and console revisions provide clearer planning and access instructions. The Index page no longer exposes the Download MDT link.

keyChanges.title: TLS 1.2 client guidance now separates the three enablement tasks
keyChanges.detail: The client article more clearly separates its three client-enablement tasks, refines the sequencing for enabling TLS 1.2 and disabling older protocols, and updates .NET Framework wording and references. It also provides clearer guidance on client readiness and registry settings.

keyChanges.title: Server-side TLS guidance clarifies .NET and architecture-specific registry steps
keyChanges.detail: The server article now uses consistent .NET terminology and gives clearer instructions for framework support, security updates, and registry subkey updates by application and operating-system architecture.

keyChanges.title: Co-management guidance distinguishes CMG from the co-management relationship
keyChanges.detail: The overview updates terminology and explanations covering co-management, workload piloting, licensing, and Entra join. It now explicitly states that Cloud Management Gateway and co-management are independent capabilities that can be used together.

keyChanges.title: The console article now says every site server always installs it
keyChanges.detail: The revised article covers opening the console, connecting to a site, authentication, navigation, and PowerShell folder management, while also updating screenshot descriptions. Its installation guidance now states that the console is always installed on every site server.

keyChanges.title: The Configuration Manager index removes its Download MDT link
keyChanges.detail: The Index page date was updated to October 26, 2026, and the Download MDT link was removed. No administrator action is specified beyond recognizing that the link is no longer present on that page.

2026-11-03.headline: Intune documents policy-only reporting for MDM Firewall and ASR Rules
2026-11-03.overview: The period is guidance-heavy, with the most operationally relevant updates covering reporting limits for MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules, device-assigned PowerShell scripts on multi-session devices, Azure Virtual Desktop Multi Session script targeting, and Win32 app delivery endpoints. The remaining edits remove a scoped-permissions general availability announcement from the Index and change an article reviewer.
2026-11-03.adminImpact: Use policy-level status when reviewing MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules. Audit device-assigned PowerShell scripts on multi-session devices, ensure Azure Virtual Desktop Multi Session scripts use device targeting with the appropriate logged-on-credentials setting, and add the two new MEM-Win32Apps hostnames to network allowlists where required. No administrator action is indicated for the Index or reviewer changes.

keyChanges.title: MDM Firewall Rules and ASR Rules report at policy level
keyChanges.detail: The Security Settings Management guidance now states that per-setting reporting is unavailable for Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM; only policy-level status is reported. Administrators reviewing these policies should use policy-level status rather than expect per-setting results.

keyChanges.title: Device-assigned PowerShell scripts cover each new multi-session sign-in
keyChanges.detail: The Windows PowerShell script guidance now states that a script assigned to a device runs for every new user who signs in, with the previous multi-session SKU exception removed. Administrators managing multi-session devices should use the updated guidance when planning device-assigned scripts.

keyChanges.title: Azure Virtual Desktop Multi Session scripts must target devices
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now requires PowerShell scripts to be targeted to devices. It specifies setting logged-on credentials to No for system context or Yes for user context, so administrators should review script assignments and credential settings.

keyChanges.title: MEM-Win32Apps allowlists gain two blob storage hosts
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoints guidance now lists mmcswdc01.blob.core.windows.net and mmcswdc02.blob.core.windows.net for MEM-Win32Apps alongside the existing hosts. Review network allowlists supporting Win32 app delivery and add the hostnames if required.

2026-11-04.headline: Co-management troubleshooting gains Windows 10 1803 requirement and token-fallback guidance
2026-11-04.overview: The period was dominated by mechanical Microsoft Learn metadata refreshes across Configuration Manager and Intune. The substantive exception was updated co-management monitoring guidance covering device-token enrollment prerequisites, fallback behavior, and diagnostics.
2026-11-04.adminImpact: For pending or failed co-management enrollment, verify devices run Windows 10 version 1803 or later and review ComanagementHandler.log. The supplied evidence indicates no mandatory configuration or migration action.

keyChanges.title: Monitor Co-management adds enrollment prerequisites and troubleshooting detail
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager guidance now states that device-token auto-enrollment requires Windows 10 version 1803 or later. If the device token fails, enrollment falls back to the user token; the page also directs administrators to ComanagementHandler.log and refreshes dashboard descriptions and image text.

2026-11-05.headline: Automatic Autopilot Policy now documents a 25-app selection limit
2026-11-05.overview: 5 November was a documentation-heavy Windows Autopilot update: the Automatic Autopilot Policy page now records a 25-managed-application selection limit, while related pages sharpen device-association behavior and sovereign-cloud scope. A separate Configuration Manager article documents a CMG bulk-registration token-verification failure and points administrators to KB remediation. The remaining edits mainly refresh procedures, terminology, links, metadata, and removed warnings.
2026-11-05.adminImpact: Use 25 as the current documented app-selection figure when planning essential Autopilot applications. Verify device association before choosing Autopilot deployment or device preparation, and do not plan device association in sovereign clouds. If CMG bulk registration uses non-Microsoft Entra joined devices, check the cited KB remediation. Apply the revised local Autopilot Reset steps where relevant, including the documented full-wipe requirement for hybrid joined and Surface Hub devices.

keyChanges.title: Automatic Autopilot Policy raises the documented application-selection limit
keyChanges.detail: The Apps section now says up to 25 managed applications can be selected for deployment, up from 10, and adds links to Enterprise App Catalog and auto-update apps. Revisit essential-application planning against the new documented limit and linked catalog guidance.

keyChanges.title: Device-association guidance distinguishes Autopilot from device preparation
keyChanges.detail: The updated page says unassociated devices run Windows Autopilot deployment, while associated devices run Windows Autopilot device preparation deployment. To run device preparation without association, it directs administrators to deregister the device from Windows Autopilot.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot overview adds GCCH and DoD scope with a sovereign-cloud limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Overview page now states that device preparation supports GCCH and DoD environments, but device association isn't available in sovereign clouds. It also explains TPM-backed association, policy precedence, corporate ownership, naming, and OOBE customization. Sovereign-cloud administrators should not plan device association.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents CMG bulk-registration token failures
keyChanges.detail: The 39169655 article now documents that bulk registration token verification can fail on the management point after installing the update rollup for non-Microsoft Entra joined devices using a CMG; other CMG communication scenarios may also be affected. Administrators in that scenario should use the referenced KB remediation.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot Reset guidance revises local configuration procedures
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed article revises local Windows Autopilot Reset configuration steps using Intune, Windows Configuration Designer, and the Set up School PCs app. It also documents the full-wipe requirement for hybrid joined and Surface Hub devices, so administrators should use the revised steps when configuring local Reset.

2026-11-06.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 disables CMG shared keys and adds Azure prerequisites
2026-11-06.overview: The 2609 guidance states that CMG storage shared-key access is automatically disabled, including for existing deployments. It adds service-principal role-assignment permissions and Microsoft.Maintenance registration requirements. Separately, Intune’s Windows bulk enrollment guidance changes token validity from 180 days to 90 days.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Before updating sites with CMGs, verify the CMG server application and operator Azure RBAC permissions at the CMG resource group, including Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor assignments, and register Microsoft.Maintenance in the subscription. Allow changes to propagate, then validate CMG deployment and client communication; missing permissions can cause HTTP 403 failures. Plan for earlier expiration of Windows bulk enrollment tokens.

keyChanges.title: CMG storage shared-key access is disabled from version 2609
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager guidance now states that shared-key access is automatically disabled for CMG storage starting with version 2609, including existing deployments. It also distinguishes storage keys from application secrets.

keyChanges.title: CMG updates require storage role assignments and provider registration
keyChanges.detail: Starting in version 2609, the CMG server application requires permission to manage storage role assignments, and Microsoft.Maintenance must be registered for the subscription. Missing permissions can cause deployment updates to fail with HTTP 403 errors.

keyChanges.title: Windows bulk enrollment token validity is now documented as 90 days
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s Windows bulk enrollment package instructions specify that bulk tokens are valid for 90 days instead of 180 days, requiring administrators to plan for earlier token expiration.

2026-11-07.headline: Recover Sites procedure now limits Services registry cleanup to Configuration Manager entries
2026-11-07.overview: A quiet period brought one targeted Configuration Manager update: the Recover Sites procedure now distinguishes Configuration Manager entries in the Services registry key from SMSvcHost entries belonging to .NET Framework.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: During site recovery, administrators should verify that each registry entry belongs to Configuration Manager before deleting it, and leave SMSvcHost entries untouched.

keyChanges.title: Recover Sites adds a safer registry-cleanup boundary
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now says to delete only Configuration Manager entries from the Services registry key and explicitly excludes SMSvcHost entries, which belong to .NET Framework.

2026-11-09.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 sites with KB39169655 need KB40345593
2026-11-09.overview: The period’s clearest operational item is a new Configuration Manager fix for bulk registration token failures through a CMG. Intune also tightened the documented authentication path for account-driven Apple User Enrollment. Most remaining entries revise Autopilot, Intune, and Configuration Manager procedures, terminology, navigation, or metadata; the revised Autopilot existing-device instructions contain one concrete procedural change.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should assess the KB40345593 update for version 2603 sites that already have KB39169655, accounting for the required site reset and manual secondary-site updates. Intune administrators handling account-driven Apple User Enrollment should use Setup Assistant with modern authentication. Teams following the Windows Autopilot for Existing Devices article should update their navigation steps and runbooks.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents the 2603 CMG token-verification fix
keyChanges.detail: KB40345593 fixes bulk registration token verification failures for non-Microsoft Entra-joined devices connecting through a cloud management gateway after KB39169655 is installed. For affected version 2603 sites, install it from Updates and Servicing; a site reset is required, existing secondary sites must be updated manually, and no computer restart is required.

keyChanges.title: Intune directs account-driven Apple enrollments to modern authentication
keyChanges.detail: The automated authentication guidance now explicitly directs administrators to use Option 2, Setup Assistant with modern authentication, for successful account-driven Apple User Enrollment. The other authentication method blocks enrollment for targeted users; the page also clarifies Company Portal, MFA, and phishing-resistant MFA guidance.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot existing-device instructions change the Enrollment Status Page path
keyChanges.detail: The revised procedure separates selecting Windows from navigating to Windows Autopilot > Enrollment Status Page, and the previous automatic-enrollment step is no longer included. Administrators consulting the article should follow the updated navigation.

2026-11-10.headline: iOS Company Portal minimum rises in December as Purview DLP adds Intune approvals
2026-11-10.overview: Two Message Center notices carry the main operational weight this period. The iOS/iPadOS Company Portal minimum will become version 5.2608.0 in early December, while Purview DLP will add Intune multi-admin approval support for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business in late November. The remaining changes are primarily documentation: new MDM partner eligibility guidance, a proxy-scope clarification, Managed Home Screen JSON guidance, and wording or formatting refreshes for enrollment and Company Portal articles.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Prepare helpdesk messaging for Company Portal update prompts and identify users whose device restrictions block app installation, since they may need to update manually. Purview and Intune administrators can expect clearer setup status, errors, and task coordination without migrating existing policies. Use the revised Setup Connector guidance when Windows WinHTTP proxy configuration is required; its wizard proxy settings do not configure the system-wide WinHTTP proxy.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS Company Portal minimum version moves to v5.2608.0
keyChanges.detail: Starting in early December, v5.2608.0 will be the minimum supported iOS/iPadOS Company Portal version for new Apple operating-system releases. Most users update automatically or receive a prompt, but device restrictions that block app installation may require a manual update process.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP adds Intune multi-admin approval support for unmanaged Edge apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late November 2026, setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will gain Intune multi-admin approval support, clearer status information, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators. Existing policies do not require migration.

keyChanges.title: Setup Connector guidance separates connector proxy settings from Windows WinHTTP
keyChanges.detail: The article now states that Certificate Connector wizard proxy settings apply only to connector services, not the system-wide Windows WinHTTP proxy. It also documents how to view, set, verify, and reset a static WinHTTP proxy.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen guidance adds JSON-based app exclusion direction
keyChanges.detail: The table entry for “Exclude these apps from the silence setting” now points administrators to the Enter JSON Data section and explains the exclusion behavior when Managed Home Screen requires authentication.

keyChanges.title: New guidance documents eligibility and application steps for MDM partners
keyChanges.detail: The new partner article describes the application process and requires eligible solutions to support MDM, user-based compliance, Microsoft Entra ID, and Android, iOS/iPadOS, or macOS. MDM vendors can use it to assess eligibility and apply.

2026-11-12.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 unpublished after group-discovery data removal risk emerges
2026-11-12.overview: Configuration Manager carries the period’s most consequential warning: release history now records that 2609 was unpublished on November 11 after an issue could unexpectedly remove discovery data for Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID groups, affecting collection membership. Separate release notes warn that ODBC Driver 18.7.1.1 can block site configuration on Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier during an upgrade to 2609, recommending validated driver version 18.6.2.1 instead. Intune updates clarify that PowerShell scripts do not block or gate Win32 app processing during ESP, document a Tunnel release upgraded to .NET 10, and revise unauthenticated proxy endpoint guidance.
2026-11-12.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should account for 2609’s unpublished status and potential collection-membership impact, and verify the ODBC driver before attempting an upgrade: avoid version 18.7.1.1 and use 18.6.2.1. Intune administrators with dependent Win32 apps should package required script prerequisites with the app rather than relying on ESP or startup ordering. Proxy allowlists supporting Intune tasks should also be reviewed against the revised endpoint list. The Tunnel update provides release and image-identification details but states no required action.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 is documented as unpublished after a group-discovery issue
keyChanges.detail: Release history now states that the 2609 update was unpublished on November 11, 2026, because it could unexpectedly remove discovery data for Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID groups, affecting collection membership.

keyChanges.title: ODBC Driver 18.7.1.1 can block site configuration during 2609 upgrades
keyChanges.detail: The release notes document that ODBC Driver 18.7.1.1 can block site configuration on Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier when upgrading to 2609. The documented validated replacement is version 18.6.2.1.

keyChanges.title: ESP guidance says PowerShell scripts do not gate Win32 app installation
keyChanges.detail: The Setup Status Page documentation now states that PowerShell scripts can run during ESP, but ESP neither tracks them as blocking workloads nor waits for completion. Startup ordering also does not guarantee that scripts finish before Win32 apps begin installing.

keyChanges.title: Intune Tunnel’s 20261026 release upgrades the agent to .NET 10
keyChanges.detail: The November 10, 2026 release documentation records an upgrade to .NET 10, refreshed Azure Linux 3.0 base images, dependencies, and VPN server components, plus diagnostic improvements and new agent and server image digests.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s unauthenticated proxy endpoint list changes
keyChanges.detail: The documented list for some Intune tasks now includes manage.microsoft.com and graph.microsoft.com, while *.azureedge.net was removed. Administrators supporting these tasks should compare their proxy allowlists with the revised list.

2025-12-29.headline: Cloud Native Windows Endpoints guide drops cloud-configuration comparison and Windows 10 notice
2025-12-29.overview: The Intune Windows guide was pared back: its comparison with Windows in cloud configuration, objectives table, links, and Windows 10 support notice were removed.
2025-12-29.adminImpact: Administrators will no longer find those comparison materials or the Windows 10 support notice on the guide page. The supplied update states that no administrative action is required.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Native Windows Endpoints guide content removed
keyChanges.detail: The guide no longer contains the tip comparing the tutorial with Windows in cloud configuration, including its objectives table and links. The Windows 10 support notice was also removed.

2026-01-05.headline: Managed Home Screen gains two RBAC permissions in Intune’s February release
2026-01-05.overview: The clearest service-facing change is the planned addition of two Managed Home Screen permissions to Intune’s School Administrator and Help Desk Operator roles. Most other high-value updates are documentation-led: Intune added or reorganized Windows feature, quality, and driver update guidance, made support boundaries and prerequisites more explicit, and documented audit-log retention as up to two years rather than one.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: Review Managed Home Screen role assignments and internal RBAC documentation as part of February release planning; no administrator action is required. For Windows update deployments, validate the documented platform, licensing, diagnostic-data, and policy prerequisites—especially the Hotpatch Arm64 preview conditions and the public-cloud and Autopatch licensing limits for Driver updates. Security and compliance teams should account for the documented two-year audit-log availability.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen adds two RBAC permissions
keyChanges.detail: The February Intune release adds TemporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen and RestoreManagedHomeScreen to the School Administrator and Help Desk Operator built-in roles. Microsoft recommends reviewing role assignments and updating internal documentation; no action is required to enable the change.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance specifies Windows 11 and Arm64 preview requirements
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance describes deploying Hotpatch through Intune and Autopatch on Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later. Arm64 support is in public preview and requires disabling CHPE with the HotPatchRestrictions=1 registry setting and restarting devices; the guidance also calls out VBS and the latest baseline release.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update policy guidance covers rollout and safeguard behavior
keyChanges.detail: A new page explains how to create and assign Windows feature update policies, configure rollout timing, manage optional or required updates, and account for safeguard holds and multi-policy behavior. It provides a documented deployment workflow rather than announcing a separate product launch.

keyChanges.title: Driver-update guidance defines licensing and environment limits
keyChanges.detail: Intune Driver updates policies are documented as public-cloud-only and requiring Intune Plan 1 plus a Windows license with the Autopatch entitlement. GCC High, DoD, and LTSC environments are listed as unsupported, so administrators should verify tenant and licensing eligibility before deployment.

keyChanges.title: Intune audit-log retention is documented as up to two years
keyChanges.detail: The Privacy Data Store Process documentation changes the stated Intune audit-log retention period from one year to up to two years for security purposes. Administrators can incorporate the longer documented availability into security and compliance planning.

2026-01-12.headline: Hotpatch and expedited quality updates anchor Intune’s Windows servicing guidance
2026-01-12.overview: Windows servicing dominates the period: new Intune guidance details targeted expedited security updates and Hotpatch deployment through Windows Autopatch, while feature-update rollout guidance separates update availability from installation timing. Microsoft Edge for Business guidance was reorganized around enrolled versus non-enrolled devices, and Windows Autopilot now records a local-reset issue tied to a specific policy setting. Most remaining changes are prerequisite, terminology, navigation, or formatting maintenance.
