keyChanges.detail: The new Intune settings reference says the baseline limits unauthorized local AI agents by disrupting common execution paths. It includes firewall rules that restrict outbound communication from runtime environments such as Node.js, plus controls that can affect Windows Subsystem for Linux and Node.js. The reference warns that the baseline may not block every execution path and may block other processes, so each setting should be reviewed and tested; it also points admins to Properties catalog inventory for Local ‌

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance changes from limited to public preview
keyChanges.detail: The setup article replaces wording that the feature was in limited public preview and available only to a select group of customers with a statement that it is in public preview, linking to Public preview in Microsoft Intune. This is a documented preview-status change, not a general-availability announcement or proof that every tenant has access.

keyChanges.title: New licensing reference maps Intune Plan 1, Plan 2, and Suite
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Intune licensing article defines Plan 1 as the base service, Plan 2 as additive to Plan 1 with advanced capabilities including Remote Help and Advanced Analytics, and the Intune Suite as additive to Plan 1 and including Plan 2. It also states that users or devices benefiting directly or indirectly from Intune need an Intune license and documents a device-only subscription. This is a new reference and does not by itself show that entitlements changed.

keyChanges.title: Account-move guidance separates regional data moves from tenant migration
keyChanges.detail: The new overview says an Intune account move relocates customer data at rest between geographic datacenter regions while preserving the tenant, policies, profiles, device enrollments, app-management state, and service configuration. It explicitly says the process is not a tenant-to-tenant migration, and distinguishes customer-requested moves coordinated through Microsoft support from Microsoft-initiated moves with advance notice. This is planning guidance, not evidence that a move is scheduled for a tenant.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance guidance now lists RHEL 10 and script sequencing
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance guide changes its listed Linux distribution from RedHat Enterprise Linux 8 to RedHat Enterprise Linux 10. It also spells out that administrators must prepare a JSON file and discovery script, upload the script to the Microsoft Intune admin center before creating the policy, and use one script per compliance policy even though each script can discover multiple settings. This is a documentation update; the supplied diff does not prove that backend platform support changed.

2026-06-01.headline: CMG image deprecation drives Configuration Manager’s Windows Server 2022 transition
2026-06-01.overview: Configuration Manager’s CMG VMSS update is the week’s most consequential change: gateways are moving from the legacy Windows Server 2022 Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`. The legacy images will lose support and image-refresh OS updates, and new CMG deployments or reimaging will fail when enforcement begins in early 2027. Intune’s substantive changes were more focused: Local AI Agent/OpenClaw inventory guidance became more specific, Apple wired-network documentation now covers iOS/iPadOS as well as macOS, and the GCC High/DoD matrix distinguishes available Windows Autopilot device preparation from unsupported update capabilities. Most other edits were documentation maintenance; the dedicated Multi Admin Approval Graph API article was removed, while Remote Help references show differing version numbers rather than a new capability.
2026-06-01.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should review CMG VMSS deployments and install KB37942646 through Updates and Servicing where applicable. It applies directly to versions 2603 and 2509, and to versions 2503 and 2409 with the required rollups; the 2509 second update rollup already includes it. CMG timing language changed during the week: an initial KB37784287 entry cited June 9, 2026, while later wording cites enforcement in early 2027, so validate the applicable current guidance before scheduling. Intune administrators collecting device properties should consider the recommended Host process field for OpenClaw discovery. Apple and government-cloud administrators should use the documented platform and cloud-specific scope, and audit automation runbooks that referenced the removed MAA–?

keyChanges.title: CMG VMSS update replaces legacy Windows Server 2022 images
keyChanges.detail: KB37942646 transitions the CMG virtual machine scale set from Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`, which does not. Legacy images will no longer be supported or receive new OS patch updates through image refresh; once enforcement begins in early 2027, new CMG deployments and reimaging operations that use them will fail. The update is available through Updates and Servicing for Configuration Manager 2603 and for 2503/2409 with the required rollups; 2509 includes itใน

keyChanges.title: Properties Catalog guidance sharpens Local AI Agent discovery
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Properties Catalog reference lists Agent Name, Install Location, Install Scope, and Host process for Local AI Agent inventory. Microsoft recommends collecting Host process because OpenClaw can run under process names such as `node.exe` or `wsl.exe`. The linked security baseline label also changed from “Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview)” to “Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw”; that terminology change alone does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Apple wired-network reference expands documented scope to iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The wired-network settings article changed from macOS-only wording to Apple devices and now explicitly covers iOS/iPadOS and macOS, with platform-specific sections and prerequisites. It states that the settings are available for all enrollment types and requires a wired network device configuration profile with the minimum Policy and Profile Manager role. The supplied diff establishes a documentation scope and prerequisite change, not a separate rollout announcement.

keyChanges.title: GCC High and DoD matrix marks Autopilot preparation available
keyChanges.detail: The government service table now marks Windows Autopilot device preparation as available and identifies user-driven deployments as available, while other device-preparation features remain in planning. The unavailable list separately names Windows Autopatch, Feature updates, Quality updates, Expedite updates, and Driver updates for GCC High and DoD. Government administrators should distinguish the available user-driven path from planned functionality.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval Graph API guidance is retired from Learn
keyChanges.detail: The dedicated “Use Multi Admin Approval with the Microsoft Graph API” article was removed. Its former guidance described opt-in access policies, interception of app-authenticated calls that modify protected Intune resources, HTTP 403 responses when required approval headers were missing, and no impact on read-only GET operations. This is a documentation retirement; the diff does not establish that MAA or app-auth enforcement was retired.

2026-06-08.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 adds internet access for Entra token validation
2026-06-08.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance, but several changes have direct administrative consequences. Configuration Manager 2603 introduces a management-point internet prerequisite for Microsoft Entra token validation, while Intune begins gradually rolling out Multiple Managed Accounts and changes the configuration path for the Managed Home Screen exit password. Configuration Manager also adds SQL Server 2025 support, and its integrated Connected Cache is slated for future deprecation. A Cloud PKI page now lists a lower CA maximum, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the service-side quota changed.
2026-06-08.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager 2603, validate management-point outbound connectivity in the system context and allow the required Entra endpoints; environments using only on-premises Active Directory authentication are unaffected. For Android Enterprise COBO and COSU devices, move Managed Home Screen exit-password configuration from app configuration policies to device configuration profiles. Verify tenant availability and the supported Teams version before planning Multiple Managed Accounts assignments. Begin evaluating standalone Microsoft Connected Cache, while treating the Cloud PKI three-CA wording as a planning signal to verify against the live service because it is supported here only by a documentation diff.

keyChanges.title: ConfigMgr 2603 introduces a management point network prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: Starting in version 2603, Microsoft Identity Service Essentials validates Entra tokens and the management point requires internet access when the site supports Entra-joined users and devices and clients authenticate with Entra tokens, typically through a cloud management gateway. The guidance names https://login.microsoftonline.com and https://sts.windows.net; if a proxy is used, it must be configured at the system level.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen moves exit-password configuration to device profiles
keyChanges.detail: For Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices, the Managed Home Screen exit lock task mode password can no longer be configured through an app configuration policy. Admins must create or update a device configuration profile to set or rotate the password.

keyChanges.title: Multiple Managed Accounts begins a gradual Teams iOS and iPadOS rollout
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune MAM capability lets users manage multiple work or school accounts in one supported app, with app protection enforced independently for each account. Current support is Microsoft Teams on iOS/iPadOS version 8.10.0 or later. One account can be MDM+MAM managed, additional accounts must be MAM-only, and multiple MDM management isn't supported.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager Connected Cache integration is headed for deprecation
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Connected Cache integration in Configuration Manager will be deprecated in a future release. After deprecation, it will receive no further feature development or updates within Configuration Manager, and Microsoft advises customers to transition to the standalone version. No retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI documentation now lists three certificate authorities per tenant
keyChanges.detail: The updated Cloud PKI index changes the documented maximum from six CAs to three for both licensed and trial tenants. It also retains the limitation that trial-created CAs use software-backed keys and cannot be converted to HSM-backed keys. This is evidence of a documentation change, not definitive proof of a service-side quota change.

2026-06-15.headline: Personally owned Android work profiles move toward web-based Android Management API enrollment
2026-06-15.overview: Android Enterprise BYOD is the week’s largest operational shift: personally owned work-profile management is moving from the Company Portal custom DPC to Android Management API, with browser-based enrollment and a documented opt-in migration path. Intune also changed Win32 content delivery to require HTTPS, made Apple ADE enrollment-time grouping generally available, and added a GCC High-only, audit-only STIG baseline. A June 2026 Message Center change moves Microsoft 365 Apps policy configuration to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center without changing existing policies. Other sampled edits mainly clarify enrollment procedures and navigation.
2026-06-15.adminImpact: Android administrators need to plan the migration and account for the Chrome or Edge requirement and the current passkey-only authentication limitation. Organizations using Microsoft Connected Cache must configure HTTPS to keep serving managed Win32 content from cache; otherwise clients fall back to the CDN. Apple ADE administrators can use enrollment-time grouping in new policies, while GCC High administrators should treat the STIG baseline as an assessment and reporting tool rather than an enforcement profile. Update Microsoft 365 Apps runbooks to use the separate admin center; existing policies remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise personally owned work profiles transition to AMAPI
keyChanges.detail: This is a transition in enrollment and policy delivery, not an immediate universal cutover. Intune is moving personally owned work-profile management from the Company Portal custom DPC to Android Management API. Administrators can enable web-based enrollment for new devices and deploy the Move to Android Management API policy for existing devices. Web enrollment uses Chrome or Edge, and if passkeys are the only accepted authentication method, Microsoft says not to enable it until web-enrollment passkey support is 신

keyChanges.title: Managed Win32 app content now requires HTTPS delivery
keyChanges.detail: This is a changed security and content-delivery requirement. When Microsoft Connected Cache nodes aren't configured for HTTPS, clients bypass those nodes and download managed Win32 apps from the content delivery network instead. Administrators relying on Connected Cache should configure and validate HTTPS on their cache nodes.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE enrollment-time grouping reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Enrollment-time grouping is now generally available for Apple automated device enrollment on iOS/iPadOS and macOS, with support in new enrollment policies. During enrollment, Intune can identify a device's Microsoft Entra security group so applicable policies, apps, and settings can be applied earlier in setup.

keyChanges.title: GCC High gains an audit-only Windows STIG baseline
keyChanges.detail: This new Intune security baseline assesses Windows devices against DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide recommendations. The initial baseline is the Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark Version 2, Release 7, dated January 5, 2026. It is read-only and generates audit reports without configuring or enforcing settings; availability is limited to GCC High tenants with Advanced Analytics licensing.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps policy configuration moves out of Intune
keyChanges.detail: This planned configuration-location change begins with Intune's June 2026 release: Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings will only be configurable in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, not the Intune admin center. Existing policies and functionality remain unchanged, but administrator guidance and runbooks should point future policy configuration to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

2026-06-22.headline: Intune’s upcoming iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 support floors demand planning
2026-06-22.overview: The period is dominated by documentation maintenance: 561 of 568 records are updates, and representative diffs largely normalize admin-center links, punctuation, and wording. The substantive exceptions are two Message Center plan-for-change notices for Apple platform support, Enterprise App Catalog auto-update guidance, a Windows 25H2 security-baseline setting, and Microsoft 365 Apps baseline version 2512. Two new Trustd Mobile articles add integration and setup guidance, but the supplied evidence does not establish a launch, preview, or general-availability announcement.
2026-06-22.adminImpact: Use Intune inventory and reports to identify iOS/iPadOS devices below version 18 and macOS devices on 14.x or below, then plan upgrades before Apple’s respective releases. Treat userless ADE devices separately because their iOS requirements differ. Review which Required Enterprise App Catalog assignments should use auto-update; Available assignments retain the existing workflow. For Windows 25H2 baseline profiles created before the June update, edit and save the profile so the new setting deploys at the next device check-in. If you use the Microsoft 365 Apps baseline, review version 2512 and its documented defaults before changing baseline plans.

keyChanges.title: Planned support change: iOS/iPadOS 18 becomes Intune’s minimum
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s iOS/iPadOS 27 release later this year, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher. The notice directs organizations to use Intune compatibility checks and reports to identify affected devices; userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment have different OS-version requirements.

keyChanges.title: Planned support change: macOS 15 becomes the new enrollment floor
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Devices already enrolled on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will no longer be allowed.

keyChanges.title: Capability guidance: Enterprise App Catalog auto-update is assignment-scoped
keyChanges.detail: Updated Enterprise App Management guidance documents automatic updates for Enterprise App Catalog apps with a Required assignment. Intune detects newer catalog versions and updates targeted devices without requiring a new app or per-update supersedence relationship. The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11 catalog apps; apps assigned Available for enrolled devices retain the existing workflow, while Guided update supersedence remains an alternative.
keyChanges.product: Enterprise App Management — Enterprise App Catalog

keyChanges.title: Changed baseline behavior: Windows 25H2 adds IE11 COM automation blocking
keyChanges.detail: The June 2026 service update added Disable Internet Explorer 11 Launch Via COM Automation to the version 25H2 Windows security baseline with a default of Enabled. Profiles created before the update do not apply the setting automatically: administrators must edit and save them, after which Intune deploys the change at the next device check-in. New or updated version 25H2 profiles include it by default.

keyChanges.title: Security baseline update: Microsoft 365 Apps version 2512 replaces 2306
keyChanges.detail: The Intune reference now documents Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise security baseline version 2512, first made available in June 2026, replacing version 2306. Listed defaults include Block Flash activation in Office documents = Enabled, Restrict legacy JScript execution for Office = Enabled, and Allow Trusted Locations on the network = Disabled. The article directs administrators to the Security Compliance Toolkit for the full 2512 settings.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise security baseline

2026-06-29.headline: Security Copilot agent guidance adds an Intune RBAC permission-delay warning
2026-06-29.overview: The supplied period is dominated by documentation maintenance rather than evidenced product rollouts: many representative edits change collection metadata, author fields, or typography. Two substantive documentation changes stand out. Security Copilot guidance now calls out RBAC permission propagation for the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, while Intune’s third-party compliance partner page replaces Kandji with Iru. Neither diff, by itself, establishes a product retirement or tenant behavior change.
2026-06-29.adminImpact: Allow several minutes for Intune RBAC permissions to take effect after adding the Vulnerability Remediation Agent’s agentic user to a group before troubleshooting access. For third-party compliance integrations, review internal references to the partner list, but do not infer from this documentation diff alone that Kandji support was retired or that Iru availability changed in the service.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance adds an RBAC propagation warning
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent page now adds an IMPORTANT note that permissions assigned through an Intune RBAC role may take several minutes to take effect after the agentic user is added to the group. This is operational troubleshooting guidance, not evidence of a new agent capability.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s third-party compliance list replaces Kandji with Iru
keyChanges.detail: The Third Party Partners page removes the Kandji entry and its Kandji Device Compliance link, replacing them with an Iru link for Microsoft Device Compliance getting started guidance. The change establishes a documentation listing change, but does not establish a Kandji retirement or a change in tenant support.

2026-07-06.headline: Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 start receiving bundled Intune Suite capabilities
2026-07-06.overview: The consequential item is a gradual rollout of selected Intune Suite capabilities into commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5: eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, with a Microsoft 365 admin center notice 30 days beforehand and no action required. The other meaningful items are documentation clarifications: Configuration Manager now spells out baseline first-evaluation conditions and Graph consent for Azure service-secret renewal, while Android web-enrollment guidance retains passkey and phone-call MFA limitations. No retirements or Message Center announcements were recorded; the remaining edits are low-impact Apple naming and macOS Company Portal procedure changes.
2026-07-06.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 administrators should watch for the 30-day admin center notice, but no provisioning action is required. Configuration Manager operators troubleshooting missed baseline evaluations should check the documented power and idle conditions and Scheduler.log. Secret-key renewal in Configuration Manager 2409 requires an account able to grant Microsoft Graph Directory.Read.All consent. For Android personal work-profile web enrollment, retain the passkey-only warning and use the documented secondary-device or SMS workaround where phone-call MFA could disrupt enrollment.

keyChanges.title: Intune Suite capabilities are being added to commercial E3 and E5
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Microsoft 365 E3 receives Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2 through the included EMS E3 entitlement. Intune Plan 2 includes Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices. Microsoft 365 E5 adds Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. The rollout is gradual, eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, and no action is required; Education and6

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager clarifies when a baseline first evaluates
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Configuration Baselines page now says that, after the first evaluation on a client, computer-targeted deployments are evaluated within a two-hour randomization window of each scheduled start time. The first evaluation on a Windows client also requires the device to be powered above the low-battery threshold and the user to be idle. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a product behavior change this week.

keyChanges.title: Azure Services Wizard guidance specifies Graph consent for 2409 renewal
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says that, starting in Configuration Manager 2409, Azure services use Microsoft Graph. Renewing the secret key requires consent for Microsoft Graph Directory.Read.All, which the Cloud Application Administrator role can't grant. Administrators must use Global Administrator or another role that can grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions. The change documents the 2409 prerequisite rather than announcing a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: Android web-enrollment guidance retains the passkey-only limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Personal work profile page removes statements that the limitation will be resolved in a future update, but still says users can't complete web enrollment when passkeys are the only accepted authentication method. It continues to advise against enabling web enrollment until passkey support is announced. The phone-call MFA caveat and the secondary-device or SMS workaround remain; no support date or behavior change is announced.

2026-07-13.headline: Configuration Manager guidance flags manual SQL collation checks before site database moves
2026-07-13.overview: Configuration Manager’s revised infrastructure guidance is the week’s highest-impact item: the Modify SQL Server configuration path doesn’t run the collation prerequisite check, so administrators must verify both the target instance and site database themselves before moving. Intune’s standout content change expands the documented custom-compliance workflow to macOS Bash discovery scripts, with a 10-minute maximum runtime and explicit format and exit-code rules. Most remaining updates are maintenance or clarification, including link corrections, support-matrix entries, and Software Center session wording. The supplied record contains no evidence of a new preview, GA release, launch, or retirement.
2026-07-13.adminImpact: Run the supplied SQL verification script against CM_<sitecode>, not master, and resolve every ERROR before using Modify SQL Server configuration; confirm that both the target SQL Server instance and site database use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. For macOS custom compliance, use Bash scripts with a valid shebang, UTF-8 encoding without a BOM, a runtime of 10 minutes or less, and exit code 0 for success or nonzero for failure. When troubleshooting software-update scans, separate forced/cache behavior from online/WSUS and offline/local-metadata behavior. Under AllSigned, use a packaged signed .ps1 with the Package and Script name options rather than embedding the script. Treat MDM Delete status Completed as server-side completion only, not confirmation that the client finished Retire.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager move guidance adds a manual SQL collation check
keyChanges.detail: The updated Modify infrastructure article adds an IMPORTANT warning that the Modify SQL Server configuration maintenance path does not run the collation prerequisite check performed by a new install or upgrade. Both the target SQL Server instance and site database must use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. A verification script must be run against the site database, CM_<sitecode>, rather than master, and every ERROR must be resolved before continuing. This is operational safety guidance, not a newly announced migration

keyChanges.title: Intune custom-compliance guidance now documents macOS Bash constraints
keyChanges.detail: The discovery-script article changes its documented scope from Linux and Windows to Linux, macOS, and Windows. macOS scripts use Bash, must run in 10 minutes or less, require a valid shebang such as #!/bin/bash, must be UTF-8 encoded without a BOM, and must return exit code 0 for success or a nonzero code for failure. The procedure adds an example that reads the Microsoft Intune Agent app version and directs administrators to set the logged-on credentials, signature-check, and hidden-notifications settings to Yes.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager separates software-update scan forcing from WSUS connectivity
keyChanges.detail: The revised Software Updates Introduction treats forced versus non-forced and online versus offline as independent decisions. Non-forced scans reuse current cached results within the TTL; forced scans always run a new scan. Non-forced online scans contact WSUS only when the cache is outside the TTL, forced online scans always contact WSUS, and forced offline scans use local metadata without contacting WSUS. The page also clarifies that one scan evaluates the whole synchronized catalog, not an individual deployment.

keyChanges.title: AllSigned task sequences should use packaged signed scripts
keyChanges.detail: A new Configuration Manager note warns that Enter a PowerShell script may not preserve signed content byte-for-byte through task-sequence XML. The signature can become invalid, causing the client to reject the script and smsts.log to record a “hash does not match” error. Under AllSigned, the documented workaround is to place the signed .ps1 file in a Configuration Manager package and reference it with the Package and Script name options.

keyChanges.title: Intune Delete status separates server completion from client Retire
keyChanges.detail: The revised action guidance states that Delete removes a device from Intune management and immediately hides it from the admin center; the Device actions report records the action as Completed. For MDM devices, Delete initiates Retire, but Completed means the server-side process is finished and does not confirm that the client device completed Retire.

2026-07-20.headline: Client-driven compliance preview centers on proactive Windows reevaluation as macOS guidance flags LAPS expiry
2026-07-20.overview: The week of 20 July was dominated by documentation maintenance: 2,515 of 2,517 recorded changes were updates, 2,482 were associated with Configuration Manager, and no removals or Message Center items were supplied. The meaningful Intune diffs describe client-driven compliance evaluation as a Windows preview, warn about macOS compliance password side effects, and document an Endpoint Privilege Management scope-tag limitation. A settings catalog tutorial also adds dynamic-group targeting references. Nothing in the supplied evidence establishes a general-availability launch or retirement.
2026-07-20.adminImpact: Windows compliance administrators should account for supported devices proactively requesting reevaluation after local configuration or security changes, rather than relying solely on scheduled check-ins; the capability is explicitly preview. Before changing macOS compliance password requirements, account for automatic password expiry across all device accounts, including LAPS and Platform SSO, and consider the documented settings catalog alternative with Change At Next Auth set to False. EPM RBAC designers cannot use scope tags with the two named roles and should use the documented Device configurations Read-permission workaround where applicable. The large Configuration Manager batch and BlackBerry edits are metadata or link maintenance in the supplied diffs and indicate no tenant action

keyChanges.title: Client-driven compliance evaluation is documented as a Windows preview
keyChanges.detail: Intune compliance-policy guidance adds “Client-driven compliance evaluation (preview)” for supported Windows devices. Devices can detect certain local state changes—including device configuration, security posture, and other compliance-affecting settings—and proactively request a compliance reevaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. This is preview guidance, not evidence of general availability.

keyChanges.title: macOS password requirements carry an all-account expiry warning
keyChanges.detail: The macOS compliance settings reference now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO. It recommends managing device passwords with a settings catalog policy and configuring Change At Next Auth to False. The diff documents this side effect; it does not establish that the behavior is newly introduced.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management roles do not support scope tags
keyChanges.detail: The EPM known-issues guidance states that the built-in “Endpoint Privilege Manager” role and the custom “Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring” role do not support scope tags. To restrict an administrator’s view permissions using scope tags, the documented workaround is to grant permissions that include Read for “Device configurations.”

keyChanges.title: Settings catalog tutorial adds dynamic-group efficiency references
keyChanges.detail: The settings catalog policy walkthrough adds links for creating simpler and faster dynamic membership rules, optimizing rule efficiency, and choosing the right targeting method in Intune. This is an ordinary documentation clarification and related-content addition; the diff does not indicate a change to dynamic-group behavior or settings catalog functionality.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Settings catalog and group targeting

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager volume is largely metadata normalization
keyChanges.detail: The supplied Configuration Manager representative diffs show mechanical metadata changes, including replacing ms.subservice “core-infra” with “core-infrastructure” and adding ms.service “microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager.” These are documentation taxonomy edits, not evidence of a product feature, retirement, security fix, or changed administrator procedure.

2026-07-27.headline: Controlled Defender configuration preview locks devices to Intune-delivered security settings
2026-07-27.overview: The week of 27 July was update-heavy—35 items were updated, one was new, and none were removed—but several changes have direct administrator relevance. Intune introduced preview documentation for controlled Defender configuration, while service release 2607 lists Samsung Knox E-FOTA and new Windows and Edge catalog settings. The Windows Sync page specifies expanded Windows processing, and Configuration Manager guidance changes the proxy context for MISE token validation. Configuration Manager’s new SQL Server page and related cross-reference edits are primarily guidance clarification. The supplied evidence does not label any of these feature entries generally available.
2026-07-27.adminImpact: Treat Controlled Configuration as a preview and note that **Off (Default)** leaves the capability disabled; review existing Group Policy, Configuration Manager, third-party, and local-script conflicts before a scoped test. For service release 2607, verify that devices use one of the listed corporate-owned Android Enterprise modes before evaluating E-FOTA, and use the documented Settings catalog path for the new Windows controls. On Windows, the expanded Sync flow and **Device sync status** tab can support troubleshooting, but the page limits this behavior to Windows. Configuration Manager 2603 management points using a proxy require Local System WinINET settings, not site-system or WinHTTP proxy settings. Also review KB 38232642 for CVE-2026-47301 and the Message Center recommendation for

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration (Device) adds a Defender authority mode in preview
keyChanges.detail: The **Controlled Configuration (Device)** setting is documented under the **Windows Security experience** profile for Antivirus policy. Its values are **Not configured**, **Off (Default)**, **Tamper Protection (On)**, and **Controlled Configuration (On)**. The new mode makes Intune-delivered Defender settings take exclusive precedence over other management channels; settings not configured in Intune use secure defaults. **Tamper Protection (On)** retains the existing secure-default behavior.

keyChanges.title: Intune service release 2607 adds Samsung firmware and Windows catalog controls
keyChanges.detail: The July 27 service-release entry says Intune now integrates Samsung Knox E-FOTA for Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with work profile (COPE) devices. Admins can select firmware versions, deploy without user interaction, and schedule downloads and installations. The same entry adds Windows Settings catalog options for camera behavior, Keyboard Filter controls for Windows Insider devices, and WSL, plus Edge 149 templates (version 149.0.4022.21) with new,

keyChanges.title: Windows Sync guidance specifies multi-workload processing and status tracking
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sync page states that selecting **Sync** on Windows initiates on-demand processing across compliance evaluation, configuration policies, app detection and deployment state, scripts and remediations, and other device-management signals. Administrators can track progress in the **Device sync status** tab in the device overview. The page explicitly says this behavior and tab apply only to Windows.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 requires Local System WinINET for MISE proxy validation
keyChanges.detail: For version 2603, Microsoft Entra token validation on the management point runs in the **Local System** context through the .NET Framework HTTP stack. A site-system proxy or machine-wide WinHTTP proxy set with `netsh winhttp set proxy` is not used. Configure the proxy in the Local System account’s WinINET settings, including `ProxyEnable` and `ProxyServer` under `HKEY_USERS\S-1-5-18\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings`, or configure Internet Options in the system context.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager hotfix guidance now identifies CVE-2026-47301
keyChanges.detail: The KB 38232642 page now explicitly says its security update for importing console extensions resolves **CVE-2026-47301**. This is updated security guidance identifying the affected vulnerability; the supplied evidence does not provide a deployment deadline or indicate a new Intune capability.

2026-08-03.headline: Multi-admin approval guidance adds app-authenticated Graph scope and policy exclusions
2026-08-03.overview: The strongest updates clarify the operating guidance for Intune Multi Admin Approval: delegated actions and app-authenticated Microsoft Graph calls are now explicitly covered, with bounded and audited enterprise-application exclusions. A related API article documents the approval response codes and resubmission requirements. Other consequential updates record a manually loaded ip_tables prerequisite for Microsoft Tunnel on RHEL 9.8, a PSSO warning for userless macOS ADE devices, and Configuration Manager 2603 media changes affecting SQL components. The remaining entries are targeted documentation corrections and clarifications.
2026-08-03.adminImpact: Review Multi Admin Approval coverage for service principals, scripts, and third-party applications; check approver-group assignments and exclusions against the documented limits. Update Graph integrations to handle HTTP 400 and 412 approval responses while retaining the original request method, URL, and body. On RHEL 9.8, load ip_tables before installing Tunnel. For macOS ADE, avoid targeting userless devices with profiles that enable PSSO registration during Setup Assistant. For Configuration Manager, validate packaging and required components if deployments depend on SQLSysClrTypes.msi or SharedManagementObjects.msi.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval guidance defines Graph-call coverage and exclusion limits
keyChanges.detail: The guidance now documents MAA enforcement for delegated actions and app-authenticated Microsoft Graph API calls. It clarifies approver permissions and direct group membership, while per-policy enterprise application exclusions apply only to app-authenticated calls, allow up to 50 applications, require second-admin approval, and are audited.

keyChanges.title: Graph API guidance specifies approval errors and resubmission data
keyChanges.detail: Missing approval headers are documented as HTTP 400. A request pending approval returns HTTP 412 with a Graph BadRequest code and an x-msft-approval-code header; callers are instructed to retain the original request method, URL, and body for resubmission.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites add manual ip_tables loading on RHEL 9.8
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisites list RHEL 9.8 with Podman 5.8.2 or later as the default and state that the ip_tables kernel module must be loaded manually before Tunnel installation.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE guidance warns against PSSO profiles on userless devices
keyChanges.detail: The Setup Assistant guidance warns administrators not to target userless ADE devices with profiles that enable PSSO registration. That combination can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected device affinity.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 media no longer includes SQL component MSIs
keyChanges.detail: The version 2603 guidance states that SQL Server Management Objects and SQL Server CLR Types use SQL Server 2025 versions, identified as SMO 17, and that SQLSysClrTypes.msi and SharedManagementObjects.msi are no longer included in Configuration Manager media.

2026-08-10.headline: Intune plans iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 floors as sync guidance broadens
2026-08-10.overview: Two Message Center plans dominate the week: Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27, and will support macOS 15 or later after macOS Golden Gate 27 releases later this year. Documentation updates mainly clarify operational guidance around device sync, registry-inventory risk, and Android Management API reporting. Two endpoint-security page edits changed only metadata dates and show no product or administrator impact.
2026-08-10.adminImpact: Prioritize compatibility inventory and upgrade planning for affected iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices, including the specific requirements for userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment. For the documented sync improvements, enable Preview new device view and monitor the Device sync status tab. Review access to registry inventory and its security and privacy implications, and use the named Android Management API report under Devices > Monitor. No action is indicated for the metadata-only endpoint-security updates.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS 18 becomes the planned Intune support floor
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center Plan for Change says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. Administrators should check device compatibility and Intune reports; userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment have specific OS-version requirements. Intune controls can be used to manage OS versions.

keyChanges.title: macOS 15 becomes the planned support floor
keyChanges.detail: After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Devices running macOS 14.x or below will remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will not be allowed. Organizations should identify and upgrade affected devices before the change.

keyChanges.title: Sync guidance documents broader processing and cross-platform status tracking
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sync guidance says selecting Sync triggers multiple workloads, including policy processing, app state updates, scripts, and remediations. Progress can be monitored in the Device sync status tab, and the guidance applies to iOS/iPadOS and Windows devices. The documented improvements require the Preview new device view toggle in the Intune admin center.

keyChanges.title: Registry inventory guidance adds an explicit sensitive-configuration risk
keyChanges.detail: The Collect Device Properties update states that registry key inventory uses existing Device Inventory permissions and may expose sensitive device configuration information. Microsoft identifies this as an accepted risk and calls for review of the related security and privacy implications.

keyChanges.title: Android Management API guidance specifies the report to use
keyChanges.detail: The updated overview directs administrators to the Personal Devices on Android Management API report under Devices > Monitor. It also clarifies that this reporting is not shown in the policy’s device assignment status or in the device configuration tab.

2026-08-17.headline: Intune’s single-device page becomes default, replacing legacy view in September 2609
2026-08-17.overview: The period’s clearest operational change is Intune’s new single-device page becoming the default in the September (2609) release, replacing the legacy page while retaining all management features. Updated guidance also documents tenant-wide device-action quotas and clarifies easy-to-misread Defender Antivirus catch-up settings. Security Copilot’s Change Review Agent documentation now carries a deprecation notice, while Configuration Manager guidance improves MBAM migration group mapping.
2026-08-17.adminImpact: Prepare administrators and internal runbooks for the September 2609 page change, and schedule large device-action batches within the documented daily quotas. Review Defender Antivirus policy values to confirm the intended catch-up behavior. Administrators using or referencing the Change Review Agent should review its deprecation notice; no deadline is supplied. MBAM migration teams can reuse existing groups when mapping them to Configuration Manager BitLocker portal groups.

keyChanges.title: The new single-device view becomes Intune’s default in September 2609
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune single device page will become the default in the September (2609) release and replace the legacy page. All management features remain available, but administrators should update internal documentation and familiarize themselves with the new interface beforehand.

keyChanges.title: Device-action documentation now lists cumulative tenant-wide daily quotas
keyChanges.detail: The updated Device Actions guidance lists daily limits of 500 Wipe actions and 1,000 each for Retire and Delete. Individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph submissions count cumulatively toward the tenant-wide totals.

keyChanges.title: Defender Antivirus guidance clarifies inverse catch-up scan settings
keyChanges.detail: Because the settings are named “Disable catch-up...”, Yes disables catch-up scans and No enables them. Full-scan catch-up is disabled when not configured, quick-scan catch-up is enabled by default, and catch-up runs after two missed scheduled scans.

keyChanges.title: Change Review Agent documentation now carries a deprecation notice
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot Change Review Agent overview now includes an agent-deprecation notice while its Intune admin center link remains unchanged. The supplied update gives no deprecation deadline or required administrator action.

keyChanges.title: MBAM migration guidance adds PowerShell group retrieval and mapping
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager’s migration guidance now explains how to retrieve existing MBAM groups with PowerShell and map them to equivalent Configuration Manager BitLocker portal groups, allowing migrating administrators to reuse existing access groups.

2026-08-24.headline: Apple DDM controls, Autopilot association, and unattended Remote Help headline this week
2026-08-24.overview: The period was dominated by mechanical Configuration Manager metadata work: 1,616 of 1,669 recorded changes, including a broad batch replacing `microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager` with `configuration-manager`. The meaningful administrator-facing exceptions were new Apple DDM App Settings and Windows Autopilot association guidance, expanded unattended Remote Help deployment instructions, the deprecation of `osVersion` for new assignment filters, and a Configuration Manager security-update procedure with explicit installation steps.
2026-08-24.adminImpact: The metadata-only Configuration Manager changes require no configuration action. Administrators should review iOS 27 Restrictions-profile migrations, validate Windows Autopilot association prerequisites and device-removal procedures, and follow Remote Help's custom-role and agent/bootloader deployment sequence when enabling unattended support. Use `operatingSystemVersion` for new assignment filters; existing `osVersion` filters continue to work. Configuration Manager teams evaluating the security update should plan for the required site reset and secondary-site recovery.

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM App Settings guidance covers supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+
keyChanges.detail: The new Settings catalog article documents allowed or denied apps, binaries, and managed-app allowances. Existing iOS app-launch restrictions configured through the Restrictions profile must be migrated because those settings are deprecated in iOS 27.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot documents TPM-backed device association before enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The new guidance describes writing tenant affinity to UEFI before enrollment, enabling device-targeted policies, device naming, OOBE customization, corporate marking, and stronger onboarding security. Administrators can pre-associate devices in Intune, assign device preparation policies, and manage association removal when devices leave the tenant.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help guidance adds Windows unattended-support prerequisites and deployment sequencing
keyChanges.detail: The updated deployment guidance covers required permissions, the Azure Virtual Desktop agent, the bootloader, and Win32 deployment. To enable unattended control, administrators must create a custom Intune role with the required permission, deploy the agent before the bootloader, and configure the bootloader to depend on the agent.

keyChanges.title: New assignment filters must replace deprecated `osVersion` with `operatingSystemVersion`
keyChanges.detail: The updated reference marks `osVersion` as deprecated: new assignment filters can't use it, while existing filters continue to work. `operatingSystemVersion` is the replacement, so no immediate migration is required for current filters.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager security-update guidance requires a site reset and secondary-site recovery
keyChanges.detail: The new page covers security fixes for the SMS Provider and administration service on Configuration Manager versions 2603, 2509, and 2503 with the required rollups. Installation uses Updates and Servicing, requires a site reset, and requires existing secondary sites to be updated manually with Recover Secondary Site.

2026-08-31.headline: Windows Autopilot policy conflicts can break hybrid-join pre-provisioning
2026-08-31.overview: The week’s clearest operational change is new Windows Autopilot failure guidance: Microsoft Entra hybrid-join pre-provisioning can fail when policy conflict resolution requires domain-controller connectivity and a bring-your-own VPN is unavailable during technician flow. Intune also expanded its in-development planning page, while Remote Help licensing and Advanced Analytics Device Query permissions received useful administrator guidance. The period was otherwise dominated by low-impact Configuration Manager metadata reclassification, with 870 of 884 changes categorized under Configuration Manager.
2026-08-31.adminImpact: Review technician-flow policies that require domain-controller connectivity, particularly where a BYO VPN may be unavailable. Audit Device Query custom roles for managed-device view and access permissions, ensure Helpers are licensed for supported Android COSU Remote Help deployments, and use the Intune in-development page to plan for upcoming enrollment, app, platform, and recovery changes. Review the Important servicing note when assessing communication with required Microsoft cloud services.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot documents a policy-conflict pre-provisioning failure condition
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues guidance says Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning for Microsoft Entra hybrid join can fail when policy conflict resolution requires domain-controller connectivity, particularly when a BYO VPN is unavailable during technician flow. It advises avoiding policies that require domain-controller connectivity during that flow.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s in-development roadmap spans app protection, enrollment, and recovery
keyChanges.detail: The page adds upcoming MHS authentication for protected app activities, declarative VPP downloads, deployment plans, Defender launch during Android setup, bulk eSIM actions, new Apple settings, and Quick Machine Recovery policies. It also documents future macOS and iOS/iPadOS support changes and the September 2609 single-device page default.

keyChanges.title: Device Query role guidance now emphasizes managed-device read permissions
keyChanges.detail: For multi-device queries, custom roles are documented as needing permissions to view and access managed devices, with Organization/Read and Managed devices/Read given as examples. The separate Managed Devices/Query permission is no longer listed.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help guidance says Android COSU Sharers need no license
keyChanges.detail: Supported Zebra and Samsung devices in Android Dedicated Device (COSU) mode don't require a Sharer license; only the Helper needs a Remote Help license. Administrators should reflect that distinction in licensing plans for supported deployments.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s servicing warning is now labeled Important
keyChanges.detail: The Servicing Information page changed its callout from Caution to Important. The accompanying message continues to cover impacts to updates, reliability, security mitigations, and feature enablement, and administrators are directed to consider communication with required Microsoft cloud services.

2026-09-14.headline: Windows Health Attestation moves to Azure Attestation by early 2027
2026-09-14.overview: Intune will migrate Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation for Windows 11 from the Device Health Attestation service to Microsoft Azure Attestation. The service-side migration is planned by early 2027 and will occur automatically.
2026-09-14.adminImpact: For Windows 11 devices using health-based compliance policies, administrators should ensure network access to Azure Attestation endpoints before the migration. Without that access, compliance evaluation may fail.

keyChanges.title: Azure Attestation becomes the evaluation service for Windows 11 health-based compliance
keyChanges.detail: Intune plans to move Windows Health Attestation from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation by early 2027. Organizations must maintain network access to Azure Attestation endpoints to preserve compliance evaluation and avoid compliance failures.

2026-09-21.headline: Windows Autopatch adds approval controls as Security Copilot joins E5/E7 plans
2026-09-21.overview: This week brought two substantive Message Center announcements: Windows Autopatch is gaining more granular update governance, while Security Copilot is now included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 plans. The Autopatch rollout runs from September 1 through October 15, 2026; Security Copilot requires no purchase or administrator action for inclusion.
2026-09-21.adminImpact: Autopatch administrators can use customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferrals, update pausing, and per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates. Microsoft 365 E5/E7 organizations receive monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools, with agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal; additional paid features remain optional.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch expands update approval and recovery controls
keyChanges.detail: Rolling out September 1–October 15, 2026, the enhancements add customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferral settings, update pausing, and detailed per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates. Administrators can use these controls to manage update timing and monitor device-level results more precisely.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot is now included in Microsoft 365 E5/E7 plans, with agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal. Organizations receive monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools; no purchase or action is needed, while additional paid features can be explored separately or organizations can opt out through support.

2026-09-28.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 raises SQL prerequisites and removes legacy Asset Intelligence reporting
2026-09-28.overview: The week’s consequential changes center on the Configuration Manager 2609 transition: stricter SQL and ODBC prerequisites and the removal of Asset Intelligence reporting components. Intune guidance also sharpens Apple DDM and enrollment boundaries, while a new Endpoint Privilege Management article documents controlled network-setting changes for standard users. Most remaining edits involve navigation, links, menu labels, and procedural wording.
2026-09-28.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager 2609 planning, verify SQL Server and ODBC versions and identify dependencies on Asset Intelligence reports. In Intune, avoid re-uploading existing VPP tokens for DDM, set the specified Automated Device Enrollment option to No, and use MDM for assignments or app configuration scenarios covered by the guidance. EPM administrators need an enabled elevation settings policy before delegating IPv4, IPv6, or DNS changes.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 now requires newer SQL and ODBC versions
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisite guidance requires ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later and SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later for Configuration Manager 2609 and later. Unsupported versions can block installation or upgrades, and the guidance identifies incompatible ODBC releases.

keyChanges.title: Asset Intelligence reporting components are removed in Configuration Manager 2609
keyChanges.detail: Starting in version 2609, Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status are removed from the Asset Intelligence home page, and Asset Intelligence reports are removed from Monitoring > Reporting > Reports. Earlier procedures apply only to version 2603 and earlier.

keyChanges.title: New EPM guidance documents controlled IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes
keyChanges.detail: The new article describes policies that let standard Windows users change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS settings while requiring confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both. Devices also need an Endpoint Privilege Management elevation settings policy enabled.

keyChanges.title: Intune warns that reusing a VPP token for DDM loses available assignments
keyChanges.detail: Re-uploading an existing VPP token for Declarative Device Management causes available app assignments to be lost. The guidance recommends a new Apple Business token for DDM, while MDM remains the path for available assignments and apps requiring app configuration policies.

keyChanges.title: Automated iOS enrollment sets a Company Portal option to No
keyChanges.detail: The Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication option must be set to No and will soon be removed. The Sync with computers setting, deprecated by Apple in iOS 13, is no longer included in enrollment policies.

2026-10-05.headline: Purview DLP will add Intune multi-admin approval for Edge unmanaged apps
2026-10-05.overview: The week is dominated by author and ownership metadata maintenance, but several updates have direct planning value. Starting in November 2026, Purview DLP will add Intune multi-admin approval for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business. Intune also documented Windows 11 version 26H2 baseline guidance, changed its endpoint allowlist guidance, and recorded a regional Remote Help limitation. Adjacent Configuration Manager documentation describes version 2609 support changes, including the removal of legacy Windows Server client operating systems.
2026-10-05.adminImpact: Admins adopting the Windows 11 26H2 baseline must create a new profile or update an existing one because current profiles do not update automatically. Network teams should reconcile allowlists with the revised endpoint table. Remote Help planners in Switzerland North must account for the Windows unattended sign-in restriction. Configuration Manager teams should identify affected legacy server clients and upgrade them. The Purview change affects setup and approval coordination, while existing policies and enforcement remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP adds a November 2026 Intune approval workflow for Edge unmanaged apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft Purview DLP will improve setup and support Intune multi-admin approval for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business. The change adds clearer status, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators; existing policies and enforcement remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Windows 11 26H2 baseline guidance now covers Settings Catalog support
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance now documents the Windows 11 version 26H2 security baseline, including new settings, updated defaults, and revised guidance. Existing security baseline profiles do not update automatically; adopting the 26H2 baseline requires creating a new profile or updating an existing one.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Security baselines and Settings Catalog

keyChanges.title: Endpoint guidance replaces regional allowlist entries with a global trouter wildcard
keyChanges.detail: The Intune endpoints table adds `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft` for all regions and removes the separate `go-amer`, `go-eu`, and `go-apac` entries. Administrators maintaining network allowlists should review them against the revised table.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help documents a Switzerland North limit on Windows unattended sign-in
keyChanges.detail: Remote Help planning guidance now states that tenants in the Switzerland North datacenter region cannot use Windows unattended remote sign-in. That regional limitation needs to be included when planning Remote Help coverage.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 ends support for legacy Windows Server client OSes
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager 2609 no longer supports Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, or their Windows Storage Server editions as client operating systems. Teams planning the upgrade should identify affected devices and move them to a supported Windows Server version.

2026-10-12.headline: Windows MDM-only enrollment DNS CNAME discovery ends January 15, 2027
2026-10-12.overview: Intune will end DNS CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment on January 15, 2027. Affected organizations will need users to enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL manually; existing devices and other enrollment methods are unaffected. Other high-impact guidance this week clarifies that Endpoint Privilege Management defaults are device-scoped, CMG VM scale set migrations need quota checks, Samsung Knox E-FOTA has a one-account tenant limit, and certain PSSO profiles should not target userless ADE devices.
2026-10-12.adminImpact: Update Windows MDM-only enrollment procedures before January 15, 2027; no remediation is indicated for existing devices. Review EPM assignments with device-wide behavior in mind, verify CMG quotas before upgrades, confirm Samsung Knox account and region alignment, and remove PSSO registration-profile targeting from userless ADE devices where applicable.

keyChanges.title: Intune is ending DNS CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment
keyChanges.detail: Starting January 15, 2027, users in organizations that rely on this enrollment method must manually enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL. Existing devices and other enrollment methods are unaffected, but enrollment procedures should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management elevation defaults remain device-scoped
keyChanges.detail: Windows elevation settings policies apply their default elevation response to all users on the device, even when assigned to a group containing users. Assigning different policies to different user groups does not create separate per-user defaults; user-group elevation rules are the supported way to vary application behavior by user.

keyChanges.title: CMG migration guidance adds Dadv6 and regional quota checks
keyChanges.detail: Before a Cloud Management Gateway VM scale set migration, administrators are directed to identify CMGs, calculate required vCPUs, check standard Dadv6 Family and regional quotas, and request increases where needed. Insufficient quota can produce a QuotaExceeded error.

keyChanges.title: Samsung Knox E-FOTA supports one connected account per tenant
keyChanges.detail: An Intune tenant can have only one connected Samsung Knox E-FOTA account, and the account and region must match the registration location of the devices. Registration can fail even when the connector reports Connected if those details do not align.

keyChanges.title: PSSO registration profiles should not target userless ADE devices
keyChanges.detail: The updated macOS enrollment guidance warns against assigning PSSO profiles that enable registration during Setup Assistant to userless Automated Device Enrollment devices, because this can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected affinity.

2026-10-19.headline: Intune’s planned device-page default changes permissions as Sync and VPP support expand
2026-10-19.overview: Intune’s main administrator-facing change is a planned switch to the new device page as the default with the September (2609) release. Microsoft says the legacy page will be replaced, device-management features remain, and admins will need the Managed devices/Update permission plus specific action permissions. Updated guidance also covers broader Sync, unlimited Apple Business and Apple School Manager VPP licensing, and a macOS lockout-timer prerequisite, while Configuration Manager clarifies CMPivot certificate trust.
2026-10-19.adminImpact: Review device-page permissions and update internal procedures for the new default experience. Use Intune’s Sync action for broader iOS/iPadOS synchronization, and deploy Apple Business or Apple School Manager VPP apps without managing license quantities. For macOS password rotation, configure Failed Attempts Reset In Minutes in the Settings catalog first when the lockout timer must be managed. In Configuration Manager, verify CMPivot certificate trust when PowerShell uses AllSigned; earlier versions require manual certificate export.

keyChanges.title: New device page becomes the default with revised permissions
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice says the new Intune device page will replace the legacy page starting with the September (2609) release. Device-management features remain, but administrators need the Managed devices/Update permission plus specific action permissions.

keyChanges.title: Comprehensive Sync covers Windows and iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune index states that the comprehensive Sync action applies to Windows and iOS/iPadOS and synchronizes key workloads such as configuration policies, apps, and scripts. Administrators can initiate the broader synchronization from the Intune admin center.

keyChanges.title: Apple VPP apps can use unlimited licenses on iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The updated index states that Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager VPP apps support unlimited-license assignment on iOS/iPadOS, allowing organizations to deploy them without managing license quantities.

keyChanges.title: macOS lockout timing requires a Settings catalog prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: Setup guidance directs administrators to configure Failed Attempts Reset In Minutes in the Settings catalog before rotating the password when they need to manage the lockout timer.

keyChanges.title: CMPivot certificate trust now has version-specific guidance
keyChanges.detail: Updated CMPivot guidance identifies the Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2011 certificate. Configuration Manager 2603 with the update rollup and version 2609 or later automatically add it to Trusted Publishers; earlier versions require manual certificate export. Devices must trust the certificate when PowerShell is set to AllSigned.

2026-10-26.headline: Intune retires legacy Apple ADE authentication in the October 2610 release
2026-10-26.overview: The week’s clearest operational change is the retirement of Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication for Apple Automated Device Enrollment with user affinity. Existing profiles are automatically updated to modern authentication, and the legacy option is no longer available. Intune also redirects iOS/iPadOS software-update management toward DDM, while Defender update controls and Autopilot app gating receive preview or capability updates. Much of the remaining volume consists of low-impact metadata and link maintenance, especially in Configuration Manager.
2026-10-26.adminImpact: Review Apple ADE user-affinity profiles and enrollment communications, although no manual migration is stated because existing profiles update automatically. Replace reliance on legacy iOS/iPadOS MDM update workloads or UTC scheduling with DDM-aligned controls. Check Intune Connector for Active Directory versions before further Autopilot enrollments, and evaluate the newly listed Defender and app-gating capabilities where relevant.

keyChanges.title: Setup Assistant legacy authentication ends for Apple ADE
keyChanges.detail: Intune states that support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication with ADE user affinity ended in the October 2026 (2610) service release. Existing profiles are automatically updated to modern authentication, the legacy option is no longer available, and new configurations should use modern authentication with just-in-time registration.

keyChanges.title: iOS and iPadOS update guidance moves to DDM controls
keyChanges.detail: Apple deprecated MDM-based software-update workloads and removed related commands with OS 27. Intune now directs administrators to Software Update enforcement and Software Update Settings, with enforcement based on each device’s local time zone.

keyChanges.title: Defender Safe Deployment appears in Intune policy guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Manage Policies page now lists Defender Safe Deployment (Preview) and Microsoft Defender AI agent runtime protection profiles. It also describes controlling when Windows devices receive Microsoft Defender updates, giving administrators a preview-stage option to assess for endpoint security planning.

keyChanges.title: Older Intune AD connectors can no longer process Autopilot enrollments
keyChanges.detail: Intune Connector for Active Directory versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 are deprecated and can no longer process enrollment requests. Version 6.2504.2001.8 uses WebView2, removing the need to disable Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration on Windows Server.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation adds Enterprise App Management app gating
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot device preparation policies can now select Microsoft Intune Enterprise App Management auto-update apps and block setup until those apps are installed, allowing required applications to be present before users reach the desktop.

2026-11-02.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 disables CMG storage shared-key access, clarifying reporting limits
2026-11-02.overview: All 3,607 recorded items were updates, and the supplied examples are overwhelmingly author-metadata maintenance rather than feature delivery. The meaningful administrator-facing changes cover CMG storage access and permissions for Configuration Manager 2609, co-management enrollment troubleshooting, Intune reporting scope for MDM Firewall and ASR policies, and revised Enterprise App Management blocking-app guidance. Configuration Manager TLS 1.2 instructions also received a terminology and procedure cleanup.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Most metadata-only edits require no action. For Configuration Manager 2609 CMG deployments, review the CMG server application and operator Azure RBAC permissions, especially permissions to create Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor role assignments. For co-management enrollment troubleshooting, verify Windows 10 version 1803 or later and inspect ComanagementHandler.log. Review MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules at policy level rather than per setting. Recheck current Enterprise App Management guidance before configuring auto-update Enterprise App Catalog apps as blocking apps in ESP or Autopilot device preparation.

keyChanges.title: CMG shared-key access is automatically disabled from Configuration Manager 2609
keyChanges.detail: The CMG security and privacy guidance now says shared-key access for CMG storage is automatically disabled beginning with Configuration Manager 2609, including existing deployments. It adds permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage, calls out Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor role assignments, and distinguishes storage keys from application secrets.

keyChanges.title: Co-management guidance adds a device-token enrollment prerequisite and fallback
keyChanges.detail: The Monitor Co-management guidance now specifies that device-token auto-enrollment requires Windows 10 version 1803 or later. If the device-token attempt fails, enrollment falls back to the user token; the page also directs administrators to ComanagementHandler.log when troubleshooting pending or failed enrollment.

keyChanges.title: Security Settings Management documents policy-level MDM reporting
keyChanges.detail: For Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM, the updated guidance states that per-setting reporting is unavailable and only policy-level status is reported.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Management removes its auto-update blocking-app restriction statement
keyChanges.detail: The revised page removes the statement that auto-update Enterprise App Catalog apps cannot be blocking apps in ESP or Autopilot device preparation. Administrators should use the current guidance when configuring those blocking-app scenarios.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager TLS 1.2 server instructions clarify .NET and architecture handling
keyChanges.detail: The TLS 1.2 server page now uses consistent .NET terminology and provides clearer instructions for framework support, security updates, and registry subkey changes by application and operating-system architecture.

2026-11-09.headline: Intune’s December Company Portal floor arrives as ESP scripting limits are clarified
2026-11-09.overview: Most of this 49-item week was documentation maintenance, but several changes have direct operational weight. Intune is preparing to require iOS/iPadOS Company Portal version 5.2608.0 in early December, while revised Apple enrollment guidance points affected account-driven User Enrollment flows to Setup Assistant with modern authentication and clarifies that ESP neither waits for PowerShell completion nor treats those scripts as blocking workloads. For co-management estates, Configuration Manager 2609 was unpublished on November 11 after an issue could remove Active Directory and Microsoft Entra group discovery data and affect collection membership.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Prepare helpdesk support for Company Portal update prompts and check restrictions that could block manual app updates. For ESP deployments, package required script prerequisites with the dependent Win32 app rather than relying on startup order. Use Setup Assistant with modern authentication for affected Apple enrollments, and factor Configuration Manager 2609’s unpublished status and collection-membership risk into co-management planning. The Purview enhancement requires no policy migration.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS Company Portal minimum becomes version 5.2608.0 in early December
keyChanges.detail: The planned minimum version supports new Apple operating-system releases. Most users should update automatically, but users affected by device restrictions that block app installation may need manual updates; helpdesk teams should be ready for update prompts.

keyChanges.title: ESP will not wait for PowerShell scripts before Win32 apps
keyChanges.detail: The revised Setup Status Page guidance states that PowerShell scripts can run during ESP, but ESP does not track them as blocking workloads or wait for completion. Startup ordering also does not guarantee that scripts finish before Win32 app processing, so required prerequisites belong in the dependent Win32 app deployment.

keyChanges.title: Affected Apple User Enrollment flows now require modern-authentication Setup Assistant
keyChanges.detail: The updated automated-authentication guidance directs administrators to Option 2, Setup Assistant with modern authentication, for successful automated enrollments involving account-driven Apple User Enrollment. The other authentication method blocks enrollment for targeted users, with additional clarification around Company Portal and MFA.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP adds Intune multi-admin approval for unmanaged Edge apps
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in late November 2026, improved setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will support Intune multi-admin approval. The change also adds clearer status information, detailed errors, and coordination between Purview and Intune administrators; no policy migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 was unpublished after a discovery-data issue
keyChanges.detail: The release notes state that the 2609 update was unpublished on November 11 because an issue could unexpectedly remove discovery data for Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID groups, affecting collection membership. Co-management administrators should account for the unpublished status and potential collection impact.

2026-01.headline: Replace “Require approved client app” before June 2026 Conditional Access retirement
2026-01.overview: January’s clearest administrator deadline is the planned June 2026 retirement of the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control; Microsoft directs organizations to “Require application protection policy” instead. A separate March change ends Microsoft Defender for Android protection of personal profiles on enrolled devices, while corporate work profiles and unenrolled devices remain unaffected. Beyond those notices, the supplied evidence is documentation-heavy but includes Configuration Manager’s MDT retirement, sharper Windows quality-update guidance, a 25-app Windows Autopilot device-preparation limit, and new Cloud PKI deployment material. The Cloud PKI additions describe cloud CA and BYOCA deployment models, CA creation, and audit procedures; they do not establish a separate January launch or general-availability announcement.
2026-01.adminImpact: Inventory Conditional Access policies using “Require approved client app” and replace that control with “Require application protection policy” before June 2026. No remediation is required for the announced Defender for Android scope change. Configuration Manager teams should remove MDT task-sequence steps before removing MDT integration. For Windows servicing, use update rings for ordinary monthly quality updates and validate the documented prerequisites before using expedited updates or Hotpatch. Revisit Autopilot device-preparation timeouts before assigning larger app sets. Cloud PKI planners should choose between a cloud root/issuing CA hierarchy and BYOCA, and verify the required CA-creation permissions.
