keyChanges.title: June retirement of the approved-client-app control
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft 365 Message Center says the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control retires in June 2026. After retirement it will no longer be enforceable; the stated replacement is “Require application protection policy,” which provides equivalent and enhanced protection. This is a planned control retirement, not a documentation-only rename.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android drops enrolled personal-profile protection
keyChanges.detail: By March 2026, Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices and focus on corporate work profiles. The notice says work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected and requires no administrator action. This is a change in protection scope and behavior.

keyChanges.title: MDT integration and standalone MDT are retired
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager release notes now state that MDT integration with Configuration Manager and MDT Standalone are no longer supported. Customers must remove all MDT task-sequence steps and then remove MDT integration to prevent task-sequence corruption and modification failures; Microsoft points to Windows Autopilot or supported operating-system deployment instead. This is a retirement with a concrete cleanup sequence.

keyChanges.title: Quality-update guidance limits expedited deployments
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance separates ordinary monthly quality updates, which continue to use Windows Update ring policies, from expedited deployment. Only eligible Windows security updates can currently be expedited; Windows versions earlier than 24H2 require Update Health Tools, and preview-build settings, non-default automatic-update behavior, notification suppression, and several Group Policy settings can interfere. This is operational prerequisite guidance, not evidence of a separate general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation limit rises to 25 apps
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device preparation “What’s new” page records a limit increase to up to 25 apps in a device-preparation policy, applying to user-driven and automatic modes, including all Cloud PC offerings. The page dates the change January 30, 2026 and warns administrators to adjust deployment timeouts when configuring more apps.

2026-02.headline: Intune reports will exclude devices inactive for 12+ months starting late February
2026-02.overview: February was dominated by Learn maintenance and clarification rather than evidenced feature launches. The clearest service-level change is a late-February reporting rule: devices inactive for 12+ months will be excluded from Intune reports. The most actionable documentation updates add an iOS/iPadOS Automated Device Enrollment MFA limitation, record Hybrid Entra join Autopilot timeout fixes, expand documented Endpoint Privilege Management support-approved request scope to all device users, and spell out Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management prerequisites.
2026-02.adminImpact: Rebaseline report dashboards after the change; Microsoft says no action is needed, but devices need to check in to remain in reports. For modern-authentication Automated Device Enrollment on iOS/iPadOS, provide an alternate MFA method because Setup Assistant doesn't support phishing-resistant MFA. For Hybrid Entra join Autopilot deployments, verify relevant OS builds include KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, or KB5070312 or later for 23H2. Before using Intune security tasks for Defender vulnerabilities, verify Intune Plan 1, Defender for Endpoint, the service-to-service connection with Microsoft Intune enabled in the Defender portal, device onboarding, and risk-assessment policies. For Endpoint Privilege Management support-approved workflows, allow for requests from

keyChanges.title: Reports will omit devices inactive for 12+ months
keyChanges.detail: Message Center says that, starting late February 2026, Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12+ months from reports to improve accuracy. Reported counts may fall; Microsoft says no action is required, and devices must check in to remain in reports. This is a changed service behavior.

keyChanges.title: ADE Setup Assistant requires alternate MFA for modern authentication
keyChanges.detail: Updated Automated Device Enrollment guidance adds a caution that phishing-resistant MFA isn't supported on Setup Assistant for iOS/iPadOS. Users enrolling through Automated Device Enrollment with modern authentication need an alternate MFA method to complete enrollment. This is an enrollment limitation and security guidance update, not a launch claim.

keyChanges.title: EPM support-approved requests are not limited to primary users
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint Privilege Management guidance says support-approved elevation requests can be submitted by all users of a device and aren't limited to the device's primary user. Administrators should treat this as updated operational scope for approval workflows.

keyChanges.title: Hybrid Entra join Autopilot timeouts map to specific OS fixes
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot known-issues guidance now lists Hybrid Entra join deployment timeouts with error 0x80004005 and identifies fixes: KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, and KB5070312 or later for 23H2. This is issue-resolution guidance, not a new deployment capability.

keyChanges.title: Defender Vulnerability Management prerequisites are now explicit
keyChanges.detail: The remediation article now uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management terminology and adds prerequisites: Intune Plan 1, Defender for Endpoint, a service-to-service connection with Microsoft Intune enabled in the Defender portal, and policies to onboard devices and enable risk assessment. This clarifies setup requirements rather than announcing a new integration.

2026-03.headline: Intune Data Warehouse reset and hotpatch defaults set administrators’ next deadlines
2026-03.overview: March’s strongest Intune signals were operational rather than a single broad release. A planned Intune Data Warehouse change threatens reporting continuity; Windows Autopatch is preparing default hotpatch behavior for eligible devices; and Windows Autopilot device preparation now supports managed-installer sequencing before app installation. Security Copilot also has a phased Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion notice, while its Vulnerability Remediation Agent is documented as a limited public preview. Much of the remaining supplied material is documentation maintenance—path corrections, title cleanup, and clarifications such as Application control remaining template-based—so it should not be read as broad product behavior change.
2026-03.adminImpact: Back up Data Warehouse data, review dashboards and queries for refreshed surrogate keys and licensing-definition changes, and move from the beta Power BI connector to the Intune admin center’s OData feed before the expected mid-June update. Identify Autopatch-eligible devices, verify prerequisites such as Virtualization-based Security, and prepare for the April opt-out setting if the May default is unsuitable. For Autopilot device-preparation deployments, review managed-installer and app ordering. For Security Copilot, track the April 20–June 30 phased E5 rollout, the allocation of 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users, and possible charges for advanced capabilities. Do not plan broad Vulnerability Remediation access: the supplied guidance limits it to select preview customers.

keyChanges.title: Data Warehouse update resets history and ends the beta Power BI connector
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s Message Center places the Intune Data Warehouse infrastructure update in mid-June 2026. It will reset historical data to about 30 days, refresh surrogate keys, and revise licensing definitions. The beta Power BI connector will be discontinued; administrators must switch to the OData feed from the Intune admin center and back up data beforehand. This is a planned change, not a completed reset.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch will default eligible Intune devices to hotpatching in May
keyChanges.detail: Starting May 2026, Windows Autopatch will enable hotpatch security updates by default for eligible Intune devices. An opt-out setting will be available from April 2026, while devices still need prerequisites such as Virtualization-based Security. Hotpatching is intended to speed security updates without requiring restarts.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation adds managed-installer support before app deployment
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows Autopilot device-preparation guidance says managed installer policy is applied during OOBE before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps install. Those app types were previously skipped to avoid installation conflicts and deployment failures. This changes application sequencing for Autopilot device-preparation deployments.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot begins phased Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion with 400 SCUs per 1,000 users
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Security Copilot inclusion with Microsoft 365 E5 will roll out from April 20 through June 30, 2026, providing 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users and core agentic features across Microsoft security products. Additional advanced capabilities may incur extra costs. This is a planned phased entitlement change, not evidence that every advanced Intune capability is included.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent remains limited to select preview customers
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance identifies the Vulnerability Remediation Agent as a limited public preview available only to a select group of customers. It uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management data to identify CVEs, prioritize remediation, and provide summarized impact analysis, suggested actions, affected systems, and step-by-step Intune remediation guidance. Administrators should not treat it as generally available; interested customers are directed to their sales team.

2026-04.headline: Edge for Business gains cross-tenant MAM as Intune’s compliance guidance expands
2026-04.overview: April’s clearest service-level change is a Message Center major update: Edge for Business now supports opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM policies for devices managed by different tenants, including app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls. The other selected items are primarily new Learn guidance or support documentation—not proof that a new feature launched. The third-party compliance list is explicitly labeled generally available, while the EPM, WSL, and Enterprise App Catalog entries provide rollout procedures and operational clarification.
2026-04.adminImpact: Evaluate the Edge capability for opt-in contractor and partner scenarios, focusing on app protection, download redirection, and leak controls. For EPM standard-user migrations, use the documented audit settings and allow 24 hours for reporting data to appear; the guide says longer observation periods may be useful. For WSL compliance, install the Intune WSL plugin, ensure the management extension can install, and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies before setup. For partner MDM and Enterprise App Catalog deployments, confirm licensing and prerequisites, preserve Microsoft-validated app defaults unless deliberately changing them, and plan around the documented update timelines.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business adds opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center major update says Edge for Business can apply Intune MAM policies on devices managed by a different tenant. The opt-in feature enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls. This is a product behavior update, not a documentation-only addition.
keyChanges.product: Intune MAM / Microsoft Edge for Business

keyChanges.title: Third-party compliance partner support is documented as generally available
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune overview labels its supported partner list as generally available, including Jamf Pro, Kandji, Ivanti Neurons for MDM, and Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM. It says partner-collected state is added to Microsoft Entra ID and that the partner becomes the MDM authority for devices assigned through an Entra user group. The documented sequence is to configure Intune and groups, configure the partner to send data, and then enroll devices.

keyChanges.title: EPM guidance prescribes audit-first migration from administrator to standard user
keyChanges.detail: The new Endpoint Privilege Management guide sets an audit-first path. Its example policy uses Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled; Default elevation response: Not Configured; Send elevation data for reporting: Yes; and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. It says reporting data can take 24 hours to return and may warrant observation over many weeks. This is rollout guidance, not a new EPM availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: WSL compliance guidance names plugin, management-extension, and cleanup prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune WSL procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Intune management extension. The extension can be installed when a PowerShell script or proactive remediation, Win32 or Microsoft Store app, or custom compliance policy is assigned. Before starting, administrators must unassign and remove existing custom compliance policies for WSL. The page documents how WSL results contribute to the host device’s compliance state; it does not by itself prove a new feature launch.
keyChanges.product: Intune device compliance for Windows Subsystem for Linux

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance sets validated defaults and update expectations
keyChanges.detail: The new Enterprise App Management procedure says Microsoft configures and confirms default installation, requirements, and detection settings for catalog apps, and warns that changing install or uninstall commands can introduce unexpected or harmful commands. It documents Windows Autopilot support for blocking catalog apps in the Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page. Most updates are expected within 24 hours, while updates requiring manual testing typically take seven days. The page identifies EAM as7

2026-05.headline: Cloud PKI documents staged CA renewal while Intune warns against trusting device-reported values
2026-05.overview: May was heavily maintenance-oriented, with 968 updates among 1,014 entries, but several diffs have concrete administrator relevance. A new Cloud PKI article documents staged certificate-authority renewal; Intune compliance reporting adds explicit warnings about unvalidated device-reported values; custom-compliance guidance replaces Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 with 10 on one supported-platform listing; Security Copilot documents delegated permissions for the Vulnerability Remediation Agent; and Windows Autopilot guidance removes the preview label while adopting Windows 365 Flex terminology. Most items are documentation or security-guidance changes. The Autopilot edit is an availability signal, not supplied proof of general availability, and the evidence does not establish a broad retirement or tenant-wide enforcement change.
2026-05.adminImpact: Cloud PKI administrators should review renewal permissions, eligibility, staged activation, and the impact of expired CAs before certificate issuance is at risk. Update compliance-reporting runbooks so Setting values are treated as untrusted context rather than enforcement evidence. Revalidate custom-compliance rollout assumptions for RHEL 8 and RHEL 10, audit the Vulnerability Remediation Agent’s delegated Intune and Defender permissions, and update internal Windows 365 references from Frontline to Flex while confirming current Autopilot availability before rollout. The single Message Center item provides no feature-level detail that warrants additional action.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI adds documented staged certificate-authority renewal
keyChanges.detail: A new Cloud PKI article describes renewal for Intune-managed and bring-your-own-CA issuing CAs. Renewal always creates a new public/private key pair, preserves access to certificates and CRLs from earlier CA versions, and can be performed through the Intune admin center or Microsoft Graph. A CA becomes eligible at half its validity lifetime or after expiration; renewal creates a staged CA that must be activated, and expired CAs cannot issue certificates until activation. The documented permissions are Read CAs andว

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance defines delegated run permissions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Security Copilot guidance says the agentic user needs delegated permissions assigned outside the Intune admin center, in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender. In Intune, the documented option is Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read; the Defender requirement is a granular custom RBAC role equivalent to Unified RBAC Security Reader. The same Intune permissions are listed for viewing results.

keyChanges.title: Compliance reports now warn that Setting values are unvalidated device output
keyChanges.detail: A new compliance-reporting section describes a Setting value column that can show information reported directly by a device, application, or administrator-supplied script. Intune does not validate or enforce the content, which may include free-form text, URLs, or file paths. The guidance says to use these values only for context, not as the sole basis for administrative action, and to independently verify links or files before opening them.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance guidance replaces RHEL 8 with RHEL 10 in its platform list
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance documentation changes the listed Red Hat Enterprise Linux version from 8 to 10. It also reiterates that administrators must prepare a JSON file and discovery script, upload the script before creating the compliance policy, and select that script when configuring the policy. This is a documentation scope and procedure change; the supplied diff alone does not prove that a service-side support retirement occurred.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot automatic mode guidance drops its preview label
keyChanges.detail: The Windows 365 automatic-mode article removes “preview” from its title, description, headings, and public-preview note. It also replaces Windows 365 Frontline with Windows 365 Flex for shared and dedicated scenarios and related links. The change signals updated availability and terminology guidance, but the supplied evidence does not establish general availability.

2026-06.headline: Apple’s iOS 18 and macOS 15 support floors top Intune’s June changes
2026-06.overview: June was mostly documentation maintenance: 680 of 698 records were updates, and many sampled diffs only normalized admin-center links, punctuation, or wording. The substantive exceptions were future Apple support-floor changes, a Microsoft 365 Apps policy-configuration move, newly documented Enterprise App Catalog auto-update scope, and a new read-only STIG assessment path. The Microsoft 365 Apps baseline page also says version 2512 replaces version 2306; the supplied evidence does not label these documentation additions as preview or general-availability launches.
2026-06.adminImpact: Use Intune inventory and reports to identify iOS/iPadOS devices that may fall below version 18 and macOS devices on 14.x or below; plan upgrades around Apple’s later-2026 releases, treating userless ADE devices separately. Update Microsoft 365 Apps runbooks to use the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center without recreating existing policies. Review Required Enterprise App Catalog assignments if auto-update is appropriate; Available assignments retain their existing workflow. DoD organizations can use the STIG baseline for assessment and reporting, but should not expect it to configure or enforce settings. Review Microsoft 365 Apps baseline version 2512 and its documented defaults before changing baseline plans.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS support requirement will rise to version 18
keyChanges.detail: This Message Center plan for change says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later after Apple’s iOS/iPadOS 27 release later this year. Userless devices enrolled through ADE have different OS requirements, so device compatibility and Intune reports need separate review. This is a future support-floor notice, not an immediate retirement announcement.

keyChanges.title: macOS support will move to version 15 and later
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release later this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will not be allowed. The notice supplies no exact enforcement date.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings move out of Intune
keyChanges.detail: Starting with Intune’s June 2026 release, Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings will be configurable only in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, not the Intune admin center. Existing policies and functionality remain unchanged, making this a change to the administration path rather than policy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance defines Required-only auto-update scope
keyChanges.detail: The updated Enterprise App Management article says Enterprise App Catalog apps can automatically update when auto-update is enabled and the app has a Required assignment. The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11; apps assigned Available for enrolled devices retain the existing update workflow, and guided update supersedence remains an alternative. This is an added documentation description, not an explicit preview or general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: New STIG baseline guidance is explicitly audit-only
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance documents a read-only Security Technical Implementation Guide audit baseline for Windows 10 and Windows 11. The listed Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark is version 2, Release 7, with 197 rules and a January 5, 2026 benchmark date. Intune assesses current configuration and provides per-setting and per-device reports through the admin center, Graph API, or CSV, with XCCDF compliance reporting; unlike other security baselines, it does not configure or enforce settings.

2026-07.headline: Commercial E3 and E5 tenants begin receiving bundled Intune Suite capabilities automatically
2026-07.overview: Most July records are maintenance edits, but the supplied diffs identify several administrator-relevant exceptions. The largest is a gradual commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 entitlement rollout: eligible tenants are automatically provisioned and receive a 30-day Microsoft 365 admin center notification. Intune also documents two previews—client-driven compliance reevaluation and controlled Defender configuration—while macOS compliance content gains a Bash workflow and an account-password warning. The evidence does not establish a general-availability release or retirement; the macOS entries are documentation and security guidance rather than proof of changed service behavior. The period’s sole Message Center item separately recommends Windows KB5101684 Preview for IT1431577.
2026-07.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 administrators do not need to provision the newly bundled capabilities; monitor the advance notification and gradual rollout. Treat both Intune previews as preview features and validate their effects in controlled scopes. For macOS compliance, check script format and runtime requirements, and assess password-expiry consequences before enabling password requirements. Follow normal Windows update validation procedures for the KB5101684 Preview recommendation.

keyChanges.title: Selected Intune Suite capabilities are being bundled into commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is gradually adding Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2—including Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices—to Microsoft 365 E3. Microsoft 365 E5 includes those capabilities plus Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. Eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, no action is required, and Microsoft will post a 30-day advance notification. This

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration gives Defender settings an Intune authority mode in preview
keyChanges.detail: The Antivirus policy guidance adds Controlled configuration for Microsoft Defender settings (preview). In the Windows Security experience profile, under Defender, Controlled Configuration (Device) supports Not configured, Off (Default), Tamper Protection (On), and Controlled Configuration (On). The default turns off both controlled configuration and tamper protection; the controlled mode gives Intune or Defender security settings management exclusive precedence over Group Policy, Configuration Manager, third-party,

keyChanges.title: Client-driven compliance reevaluation is documented as a Windows preview
keyChanges.detail: Supported Windows devices can detect certain local state changes—including device configuration and security-posture changes—and proactively request a compliance reevaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. Administrators should account for this alternate evaluation timing when interpreting compliance results; the supplied evidence labels the capability preview and does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance guidance adds macOS Bash scripts and strict execution requirements
keyChanges.detail: The custom compliance discovery-script procedure now documents macOS alongside Linux and Windows. macOS scripts use Bash, must run in 10 minutes or less, include a valid shebang, be UTF-8 encoded without a BOM, and return exit code 0 for success or a non-zero code for failure. This is a documentation expansion; the supplied diff does not establish a new service rollout.

keyChanges.title: macOS compliance guidance warns that password requirements expire every device account
keyChanges.detail: The macOS compliance reference now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO. It recommends managing device passwords through a settings catalog policy with Change At Next Auth configured to False. This is security guidance and a behavior clarification, not evidence that the service behavior newly changed.

2026-08.headline: Apple DDM app-setting guidance lands as Intune plans iOS 18 and macOS 15 floors
2026-08.overview: Apple is the clearest Intune theme this month: new Settings catalog guidance covers Apple DDM App Settings for supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+, while Message Center plans future minimums of iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 after Apple’s 27 releases. Windows Autopilot also gains documented TPM-backed device association guidance. Intune’s Remote Help plan now defines unattended sessions for Windows and Android, and the assignment-filter reference replaces deprecated `osVersion` for new filters with `operatingSystemVersion`. Much of the remaining volume was a broad Configuration Manager metadata reclassification; the substantive exception was security-update guidance requiring a site reset and secondary-site recovery.
2026-08.adminImpact: Inventory Apple devices and use Intune reports and OS-version controls to plan the upcoming enrollment floors. Existing macOS 14.x-and-earlier devices remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will be blocked after the macOS change; userless Automated Device Enrollment devices have separate iOS/iPadOS requirements. For supervised Apple devices, configure the documented DDM controls through the Settings catalog and migrate iOS app-launch restrictions from Restrictions profiles because those settings are deprecated in iOS 27. Use `operatingSystemVersion` for new assignment filters; existing `osVersion` filters continue to work. Before adopting unattended Remote Help, review helper roles, Conditional Access, and privacy implications. Configuration Manager administrators applying1

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM App Settings adds app and binary controls
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance covers Settings catalog configuration for supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+, including allowed or denied apps, binaries, and managed-app allowances. Existing iOS app-launch restrictions in the Restrictions profile must be migrated because those settings are deprecated in iOS 27.

keyChanges.title: Intune plans an iOS/iPadOS 18 minimum after iOS/iPadOS 27
keyChanges.detail: Message Center says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. Organizations should check device compatibility and Intune reports, including the separate requirements for userless Automated Device Enrollment devices, and use Intune controls to manage OS versions.

keyChanges.title: macOS enrollment moves to a macOS 15 minimum after Golden Gate 27
keyChanges.detail: After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will not be allowed; affected devices should be identified and upgraded before the change.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot documents TPM-backed device association
keyChanges.detail: The new overview describes writing tenant affinity to UEFI before enrollment, enabling device-targeted policies, device naming, OOBE customization, corporate marking, and stronger onboarding security. Administrators can pre-associate devices in Intune and manage association removal when devices leave the tenant.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager security update requires a site reset
keyChanges.detail: The security-update guidance applies to Configuration Manager versions 2603, 2509, and 2503 with required rollups. Installation uses Updates and Servicing, requires a site reset, and requires administrators to use Recover Secondary Site to update existing secondary sites.

2026-09.headline: Intune’s Windows Health Attestation migration requires Azure endpoint access by early 2027
2026-09.overview: September’s most consequential Intune change is the planned migration of Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation for Windows 11 from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation. The service-side migration is automatic, but affected environments need network access to Azure Attestation endpoints. Intune also gained more granular Windows Autopatch approval and reporting controls, while Security Copilot became included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 plans. Most remaining activity was Configuration Manager documentation maintenance, with meaningful 2609 guidance covering SQL prerequisites and the removal of Asset Intelligence reporting.
2026-09.adminImpact: Prioritize Azure Attestation endpoint access for Windows 11 devices using health-based compliance policies. Review Windows Autopatch approval, deferral, pause, and reporting options during its September 1–October 15 rollout. For Configuration Manager 2609 plans, validate SQL Server and secondary-site Visual C++ prerequisites and assess dependencies on Asset Intelligence reports. Microsoft 365 E5/E7 organizations receive Security Copilot, monthly Security Compute Units, and developer tools without a new purchase or required action.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation is moving to Microsoft Azure Attestation
keyChanges.detail: Intune plans to migrate Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation for Windows 11 from the Device Health Attestation service to Microsoft Azure Attestation by early 2027. The migration occurs automatically on the service side, but organizations must provide network access to Azure Attestation endpoints or health-based compliance evaluation can fail.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch adds granular approval and recovery-update controls
keyChanges.detail: Rolling out from September 1 through October 15, 2026, the enhancements add customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferral settings, update pausing, and per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 guidance raises the SQL Server support floor
keyChanges.detail: The updated support guidance marks SQL Server 2016 and SQL Server 2016 Express as deprecated in version 2609. SQL Server editions earlier than SQL Server 2017 CU2 must be upgraded before installing or updating to 2609, and the Visual C++ Redistributable on secondary sites must also be updated.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 removes documented Asset Intelligence reporting
keyChanges.detail: The updated operations guidance says that, starting in version 2609, the Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status sections and Asset Intelligence reports are removed. Procedures on the page apply to version 2603 and earlier, so administrators should review reporting dependencies before upgrading.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot is now included in Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 plans, with monthly Security Compute Units, developer tools, and agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal. No purchase or administrator action is required for the included capability; additional paid features remain optional.

2026-10.headline: Intune ends Windows CNAME discovery and retires legacy Apple ADE authentication
2026-10.overview: October’s substantive Intune changes shift administrators away from legacy enrollment and update paths. Windows MDM-only enrollment will lose DNS CNAME auto-discovery on January 15, 2027; Apple ADE user-affinity enrollment dropped Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication in the 2610 release, and Apple OS 27 removed MDM software-update commands in favor of DDM. Intune also published Windows 11 26H2 baseline guidance and tightened the Autopilot Connector version boundary, while many other supplied updates were link or metadata maintenance.
2026-10.adminImpact: Update Windows MDM-only enrollment procedures before January 15, 2027; existing devices and other enrollment methods are unaffected, but users will need to enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL manually. Review Apple ADE enrollment communications and use modern authentication with just-in-time registration for new configurations; existing legacy profiles update automatically. For Apple OS 27, use DDM-based Software Update enforcement and Software Update Settings, accounting for each device’s local time zone. Create or update a Windows 11 26H2 baseline profile rather than expecting existing profiles to change automatically, and upgrade any Intune Connector for Active Directory older than version 6.2501.2000.5.

keyChanges.title: Windows MDM-only enrollment loses CNAME auto-discovery on January 15, 2027
keyChanges.detail: Intune will end support for DNS CNAME auto-discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment. Users will need to enter the Microsoft enrollment server URL manually; existing devices and other enrollment methods are unaffected.

keyChanges.title: Setup Assistant legacy authentication ends for Apple ADE user affinity
keyChanges.detail: Support for Setup Assistant (legacy) authentication with Automated Device Enrollment user affinity ended in the October 2026 (2610) service release. Existing profiles are automatically updated to modern authentication, and the legacy option is no longer available.

keyChanges.title: Apple OS 27 moves software-update control from MDM commands to DDM
keyChanges.detail: Apple deprecated MDM-based software-update workloads and removed related commands with OS 27. Intune now directs administrators to Software Update enforcement and Software Update Settings, with enforcement based on each device’s local time zone.

keyChanges.title: Windows 11 26H2 baseline adoption requires explicit profile changes
keyChanges.detail: Intune now documents the Windows 11 version 26H2 security baseline and Settings Catalog support, including new settings and updated defaults. Existing security baseline profiles do not update automatically; administrators must create a new profile or update an existing one to adopt the guidance.

keyChanges.title: Older Intune AD connectors can no longer process Autopilot enrollments
keyChanges.detail: Intune Connector for Active Directory versions older than 6.2501.2000.5 are deprecated and can no longer process enrollment requests. Version 6.2504.2001.8 uses WebView2, so Windows Server no longer requires Internet Explorer Enhanced Security Configuration to be disabled.

2026-11.headline: Intune sets Company Portal v5.2608.0 as December iOS/iPadOS minimum
2026-11.overview: November was overwhelmingly documentation maintenance: 3,652 items were updated and two were new, with many representative edits limited to metadata, links, terminology, or wording. The substantive exceptions included the early-December Company Portal version floor, Configuration Manager 2609 CMG storage-access guidance, a Purview DLP workflow update involving Intune approval, and clearer Intune reporting and Enterprise App Management guidance.
2026-11.adminImpact: Prepare helpdesk staff for Company Portal update prompts and check device restrictions that could block manual updates. For Configuration Manager 2609 CMG deployments, review the CMG server application and operator Azure RBAC permissions. Use policy-level status when assessing MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules, and review the current Enterprise App Management guidance before configuring blocking apps for ESP or Autopilot device preparation. No Purview policy migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Company Portal minimum becomes v5.2608.0 in early December
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says the minimum iOS/iPadOS Company Portal version will become v5.2608.0 in early December to support new Apple operating-system releases. Most users update automatically; others receive prompts, while device restrictions that block app installation may require manual-update support.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 disables CMG storage shared-key access
keyChanges.detail: CMG security guidance now states that shared-key access is automatically disabled for CMG storage beginning with Configuration Manager version 2609, including existing deployments. It adds permissions for Microsoft Entra-authenticated storage, including Storage Blob Data Contributor and Storage Table Data Contributor role assignments, and distinguishes storage keys from application secrets.

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP adds Intune multi-admin approval for unmanaged Edge apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late November 2026, improved setup and activation for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business will add Intune multi-admin approval, clearer status, detailed errors, and task coordination between Purview and Intune administrators. No policy migration is required.

keyChanges.title: MDM Firewall and ASR reporting is limited to policy status
keyChanges.detail: Security Settings Management guidance now states that per-setting reporting is unavailable for Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM; only policy-level status is reported. Administrators should interpret status for these policies at the policy level.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Management revises ESP blocking-app guidance
keyChanges.detail: The current page no longer states that auto-update Enterprise App Catalog apps cannot be blocking apps in Enrollment Status Page or Autopilot device preparation. Administrators configuring blocking apps in those workflows should follow the revised guidance.
